sections.text: Browser Router BrowserRouter maps the current browser URL to a page and replaces only therouter’s content when navigation occurs. It uses the History API, handlesinternal links, and responds to browser back and forward actions.

sections.title: Define routes and mount the router
sections.text: Define routes and mount the router A route handler provides a path and a page factory. A page contains its DOMroot and can optionally provide a title, description, and initialization hook. The router should normally be created once for the application and mounted tothe element that owns the page content. See the BrowserRouter API reference.

DataForm DataForm edits one object at a time. It reuses DataViewField metadata andthe same field-editor factory as DataGrid, so display formatting, validation,lookups, dates and numeric editors behave consistently in both components.

sections.title: Plain objects and DataRow
sections.text: Plain objects and DataRow Pass a plain object to get an isolated draft. The original object is unchangeduntil the host accepts the form’s value. When the value is a DataRow, theform detects its row contract and writes accepted values through row.setValue,so the table receives normal change notifications and tracking. Click a value, press Enter or F2, edit it and confirm with Enter.Escape restores the accepted value. Leaving the editor commits it afterasynchronous validation; a rejected value keeps its editor and error visible.While editing, Enter and Tab commit and move to the next editable field;Shift+Tab moves to the previous field. Escape cancels the field andreturns focus to its cell. An open lookup or date popup keeps ownership of itsown keyboard commands until it closes.

sections.title: Labels and adapters
sections.text: Labels and adapters Use labelPosition: "top" (the default) or "start" for compact horizontalforms. Both forms accept the same DataViewField definitions. Supply adapterwhen a domain object does not expose field values directly; the adapter onlyneeds getValue, getText, and setValue. For plain objects, the built-in adapter edits a shallow draft. For DataRow,the built-in adapter preserves the table’s mutation pipeline. Use onCommit forside effects or remote persistence after a field has been accepted.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataForm,DataFormOptions,DataFormAdapter, andDataViewField.

Copy and paste Copy works without enabling editing. Select a range and use Ctrl+C / Command+C or the context-menu Copy command. Copy with headers adds column captions. Clipboard text follows the field display text; a display format is not necessarily lossless. Paste requires an editable grid and an updating source. Try it in the array and lookup demo.

sections.title: Pasting cells
sections.text: Pasting cells With allowEdit: true, Ctrl+V / Command+V pastes tab-separated text at the activecell. Inside an editor, paste remains the editor’s native text operation. Theblock is not repeated to fill a larger selection. Read-only fields are skippedwithout shifting columns; fields beyond the last visible column are ignored.Group and summary rows cannot be paste destinations. Select the starting cell with a single click, then use Ctrl+V / Command+V orright-click and choose Paste. The context-menu command reads text from thesystem clipboard and uses the same pipeline as keyboard paste. Browser permissionmay be required; if reading is unavailable or denied, the menu offers a return tothe grid with an instruction to use keyboard paste. Copy and Copy with headersare also available in the context menu. Include "paste" instandardContextMenuItems when supplying an explicit list of built-in commands. Each cell uses its editor’s resolveTextand validation. Lookup text must resolve unambiguously unless a custom resolveraccepts free text. Successfully resolved fields are sent in one update per row;failed cells retain their text and error, and the next input row is processed.There is no whole-paste rollback for a general remote source. Input extending past the result creates independentNewRowSession instances. Failure to create anew row stops the remaining paste, retaining earlier results. A cell failure keepsits row pending without calling insert(), and processing continues. An insertfailure also retains the session and its error and continues to the next row.Correct pending rows in place, then leave them to retry insertion, or useinsertNewRow(session) explicitly. The same operation is available programmatically. In the array example, selectthe Description column first so the following three values align withDescription, Product and Quantity: pasteText waits for processing to finish;cell and insert errors are retained rather than rejecting its promise. Creation,query and malformed clipboard errors reject. Paste is serialized and grid editingis unavailable until it settles. Grid-level undo/redo shortcuts remain separate;source-owned history decides which mutations can be undone.

Columns and sizing Columns define how a DataGrid reads, displays, and lays out each field. Usecaptions for user-facing labels and keep field names focused on the data model. Grid definitions use DataGridColumn, whichextends DataViewField andDataField. Common labels, value access and formattingcan be shared with other views; width, alignment, resize/reorder, context menusand custom cell rendering belong to the grid column.See Fields and presentation for the three layers. The demo combines explicitly sized columns with an automatic Product column andpinned columns. Switch the width mode and resize the container to compare thebehavior. Use Manual resize to compare resizing only one column with changingits neighbor too. Column headers can also be reordered directly.

sections.title: Column width modes
sections.text: Column width modes columnWidthMode controls how spare container space is distributed: Mode Behavior fixed Keeps configured or content-measured base widths without stretching. stretch-auto Proportionally stretches only columns without a configured width. This is the default. stretch-all Proportionally stretches all data columns, including explicitly sized and pinned columns. The row header keeps its width in all modes. Stretch modes only expand: when thebase widths exceed the viewport, horizontal scrolling remains available. Forexample, widths of 100 and 200 become 200 and 400 in a 600px viewport without a rowheader. Proportions are always calculated from base widths, not the previousstretched result, so repeated container resizing does not accumulate changes. getColumn().width stores a base width, which may differ from the stretched widthshown on screen. Returning to fixed restores base widths. UseautoSizeColumn(name) to return a manually sized column to content measurement. Automatic measurement has an 80px minimum and includes the text in loaded bodyrows and the visible total footer. Footer labels for multiple aggregates areincluded too. Totals arriving later, or changing after a query, may grow an autocolumn but do not shrink its measured data baseline. Hidden footers are excluded.The grid measures loaded rows, not the entire dataset. A nonempty data cell doesnot force a long caption to fit; the caption remains a fallback for empty cells.Explicit widths (including widths below 80px) and manual resizing retain theirown behavior. Use autoSizeColumn(name) to measure again after manual sizing.

sections.title: Manual column resizing
sections.text: Manual column resizing columnResizeMode controls dragging a header separator independently ofcolumnWidthMode: Resize mode Behavior next-column Exchanges width with the next visible data column. All other columns stay still and the pair’s total width is unchanged. independent Changes only the dragged column. The inner table can grow or shrink; the outer grid container keeps its width. Horizontal scrolling appears when needed. When omitted, columnResizeMode follows the width mode: next-column forstretch-auto and stretch-all, and independent for fixed. An explicit resizemode overrides that choice. Set it to undefined to restore the automatic choice.The choice depends on the configured width mode, not CSS percentages or whethera horizontal scrollbar is currently visible. The next column is the next visible data column, including pinned columns;hidden columns and the row header do not participate. The last visible columnresizes independently because it has no neighbor. Interactive widths are boundedby 40–800 CSS pixels; a pair stops when either column reaches its bound. Existingwidths outside those bounds do not jump into range when a drag starts. Dragging changes only the affected columns’ base widths and removes them from theautomatic pool in stretch-auto. In stretch-all, their proportional weightsare updated. Other columns retain their configured widths and auto eligibility.Rendered widths remain stable during dragging, after release and on repaint;shrinking independently does not immediately refill the freed space. An actual viewport-width change or an explicit layout rebuild (for example,changing column widths, visibility, pinning or width mode) resumes normalcolumnWidthMode distribution from the base widths. Escape, window blur andtouch cancellation restore the layout from before the gesture. Clicking aseparator without moving it does not configure a width or disable auto sizing. The vertical scrollbar starts below the entire fixed table header, includingthe filter row and sticky group/tree rows, keeping the last column’s right-handresize handle accessible even while the scrollbar is expanded. API: ColumnResizeMode,DataGridOptions.columnResizeMode. Use setColumnOptions() for a single column and setOptions() for layout-widechanges such as visibleColumns, fixedLeftColumns, and fixedRightColumns.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGridColumn,DataViewField andDataGridOptions.

Context menus DataGrid exposes separate customization points for cells, rows, row headers,and column headers. Keep standard actions and add application-specific actionswhere they are relevant. The demo adds a custom row action while retaining the built-in column menu.Context callbacks receive the row, column, selected ranges, and originatingmouse event.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGridContextMenuContext,GridContextMenuItems, andGridStandardContextMenuItem.

Appearance and custom rendering DataGrid uses the root class elg-data-grid, row classes elg-data-grid-row-*and cell classes elg-data-grid-cell-*. These are separate from the elg-gridlayout utility. Cell color tokens such as --elg-data-grid-cell-bg keep their names. Use renderCell when the default text representation is not enough. Therenderer returns the content for the cell, while DataGrid continues to ownselection, hover, dragging, and other cell states.

sections.title: Borders, hover and cursor
sections.text: Borders, hover and cursor These options change presentation, not selection or editing capabilities: Option Values and default showBorder Outer frame; true by default, including the group panel cellBorders none, rows (default) or all showRowHover Row hover background; false by default showSelection Selection highlighting; true by default, independent of selection state cursor default (default), pointer or text Cell border modes reserve the same geometry, using transparent separators whenhidden, so changing modes does not resize cells or shift an editor. Selection anderror indicators remain independent of ordinary separators. Pending new rowsretain their separate status; see new rows. Use semantic tokens and CSS custom properties rather than theme-specific coloroverrides. The DataGrid token prefix is --elg-data-grid-, distinct from the layoutgrid’s --elg-grid- variables. Try the border controls in theediting demo.

sections.title: Custom content and state-aware styling
sections.text: Custom content and state-aware styling Use customCellStyle to style the outer grid cell. In particular,--elg-data-grid-cell-bg is the base background used by DataGrid when it mixes acell state such as selection with the custom color. The renderer below returns a VNode for the status text. Ready cellsuse a soft green base color, while Delayed cells use a muted red one. Thestatus text is also rendered in uppercase. Select one or more cells to see theselection border and background tint applied without changing the renderer’stext. renderCell receives a GridCell with the column, raw value, display text,the render-ready gridRow, and the original rowData when the cell belongs toa data row. Group rows do not have one original data row, so rowData isundefined; use value, text, and gridRow instead. The renderer must returna virtual node. The VNode becomes the content inside the grid cell wrapper, soDataGrid can preserve its own selection, hover, and interaction behavior. customCellStyle affects the outer .elg-data-grid-cell, not only the returnedcontent. This is important because the grid can then apply state styling to acustom green or red background. The renderer does not need to know howselection or hover colors are implemented.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGridColumn, GridCell,DataViewField, DataCell,and DataCellStyle for the completerenderer and style contracts.

Connecting data The grid consumes a DataSource contract rather than depending on a specificstorage technology. ArrayDataSource is useful for local data; an applicationcan implement loadData() for an API, database, or service layer. The same grid options work with both local and remote sources. Queries carryfiltering, sorting, grouping, paging, and an AbortSignal for cancelled loads.

sections.title: Editing an array source
sections.text: Editing an array source ArrayDataSource implements the optional editing methods of DataSource.update() changes the actual row object, and delete() removes it from the suppliedarray. Changes are immediate and local; there is no batch save or undo history.Use DataSet when you need transactions, undo or a batch to persist. API: ArrayDataSourceOptions,update(),delete(),createNewRow(),NewRowSession. New rows are plain objects. The identity field defaults to id; configureidField for another member. The generated identity overrides a default valuefor that member and cannot be changed through update(). Multiple drafts cancoexist; duplicate identities are rejected. Defaults and identity factories canbe asynchronous. Insertion keeps the same row reference and identity. The changed event reports create,update, insert, delete and cancel. Equal-value updates and repeatedsuccessful insert/cancel calls emit no additional event. Direct external editsto the public array or its objects do not emit this event.

sections.title: Grouping adapters preserve editing capabilities
sections.text: Grouping adapters preserve editing capabilities LocalGroupingDataSource delegatesupdate, delete, createNewRow, row identity and hierarchy methods only whenthe wrapped source supplies them. A read-only source therefore stays read-only.New-row sessions belong to the original source, not to the adapter. The adapter exposes the original changed event and undoCoordinator.Wrapping a DataTable preserves its dataset transactions and history; wrappingan ArrayDataSource does not introduce history or persistence.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataSource,ArrayDataSource, andGridDataSource.
Change tracking and saving

sections.title: DataTable and business rules
sections.text: DataTable and business rules The grid uses exactly the same update command with DataTable.These are local, undoable changes; persistence remains the application’s job.The example’s total is calculated by a business rule in the same transaction.Undo and redo are external buttons, not a second grid-owned history.

sections.title: Modified cells
sections.text: Modified cells Sources may implement isCellModified(row, fieldName)to expose differences from their accepted/persisted baseline. The grid reads thissynchronous capability when rendering; it owns no second change buffer. Sourceswithout it, including ArrayDataSource, do not display modification marks.DataTable.isCellModified delegatesto DataRow.isModified, including customequality, business-rule changes, and undo/redo. Source changed notificationsrefresh the cells. A failed save retains the marks; a successfulsaveChanges accepts the baseline andclears them. The demo’s Save (simulated) makes no network request. Pending sessions retain only their * and green bottom edge. After insertion,unsaved added rows mark every present field, including default values. The emptyplaceholder, row headers, group rows and summaries have no modified-cell tint. The background order is custom base, then a 10% success tint, then selection.Error outlines remain independent. Override --elg-data-grid-modified-cell-bgto replace the modified background. Use the base token for custom colors thatshould participate in normal tinting: Direct background or backgroundColor styles explicitly override the computedbackground, including its modification and selection tints. A custom sourceshould emit changed after changing modification state or accepting a save;the grid does not infer persistence from an update event.
New rows and pending sessions Use the cell editing demo to add several pending rows and inspect their sessions. The same demo exercises every border mode and the per-session Insert/Cancel commands.

sections.title: Adding rows
sections.text: Adding rows An editable source with createNewRowand update displays one input row at the end of the result. Its row header shows*. Customize its label through texts.newRowText. Merely selecting thisplaceholder creates no data. Starting an edit waits for createNewRow() beforecreating the editor, so defaults, lookup providers and validators receive the realdomain row. Typing during asynchronous initialization is retained. Confirming cells calls update(session.row, values) without inserting the row.The pending row remains outside the query’s filtering, sorting and totals.Moving to another row attempts session.insert() unless the row has rejectedcell input. A row with errors remains pending but does not block navigation orcreation of another new row. All pending rows appear after query rows, each with* in its header and a subtle line along the bottom of its cells; the final emptyplaceholder is available for another new row and has no pending-row line.The bottom border of data cells uses the success color at 30% opacity, includingwhen cell borders are hidden. Row headers retain the configured grid borders.Border modes change colors without changing cell dimensions;selection and error outlines remain independent inside the cells.Override --elg-data-grid-pending-row-border-colorto customize its color. Use the demo’s Cell borders selector to compare noseparators, row separators, and full cell borders. Outer border controls thegrid’s surrounding frame independently.Enter at the bottom boundaryalso inserts; Tab does so at the last column. Successful insertion refreshes thequery and presents a fresh placeholder. cellNavigating.cancel prevents both themove and automatic insertion. A failed insert retains the session and values. Its error is exposed throughnewRowError and the input cells’ tooltip.Correct the row and retry. Escape first discards invalid input on the active cell,whether its editor is open or closed. If that cell has no error, Escape cancelsthe whole pending row. The context-menu Cancel new row and explicitcancelNewRow(session) always cancel the whole session. No new session is createdfor each subsequent cell. Initialization or insertion in progress blocks anotheredit; insertion requests are coalesced.

sections.title: Managing new-row sessions
sections.text: Managing new-row sessions newRowSessions is a read-only snapshotof the pending NewRowSession objects createdthrough this grid. These are the actual source sessions, not grid wrappers. Theirobject identity survives view reloads and reordering. Creating another sessiondoes not mutate an earlier snapshot. Completed sessions leave the grid’s collection;references held by the application still expose their terminal state. Use the grid API when UI input must be respected: createNewRow() delegates initializationto the source, registers the session and displays its domain row. Placeholderediting and paste share the same registration path. It rejects if creation fails,the source does not support editing, or a conflicting operation is running. insertNewRow(session) finishes a celleditor belonging to that session, then refuses insertion if the row has retainedinvalid input. It delegates domain validation to session.insert() and retainssource errors for correction. It does not revalidate every untouched field: enforcewhole-row business rules in the source. cancelNewRow(session)discards that row’s editor, calls session.cancel() and clears only its input/errors.Neither method finishes or cancels an editor belonging to another row; a viewreload is deferred until that editor closes. Both methods require an explicit session owned by this grid. A foreign or alreadycompleted session rejects with an error. Expected validation/source failures andconflicting commands return false, leaving the row pending. Identical in-flightcommands for the same session share one promise; an insert and cancel cannot runconcurrently. Initialization and paste also block conflicting row commands. The grid’s keyboard navigation, automatic insertion on leaving a pending row,Escape and Cancel new row context-menu command use these same session-aware paths.No visible index or implicit selection is used by the public row commands.

sections.title: Direct source commands
sections.text: Direct source commands Calling the source session directly deliberately bypasses grid input handling: The two commands above address different sessions; an inserted row cannot be cancelled.For automatic UI updates, the source must emitchanged after a successful insert orcancel and expose the updated session state. The grid removes that session,clears its retained input and closes only its editor. Without source notifications,direct commands do not guarantee a synchronized grid. The grid’s own methods updatetheir collection/view even if the optional event is absent. Source sessions createdelsewhere are not automatically adopted by this grid.

sections.title: Completing several rows
sections.text: Completing several rows Snapshot iteration is safe while commands remove sessions: endEdit and cancelEdit() still operate ononly the active cell; cancelEdit() also clears its retained invalid input/errorand never cancels a whole row. Escape adds the pending-row cancellation prioritydescribed above. hasPendingNewRow reports whether anypending rows remain. Query/source/column changes require all sessions to beinserted or cancelled first. Disposal cancels all owned pending sessions afterin-flight operations finish. Inserting into a DataTable is alocal change; saving the DataSet remains a separate application command. See beginEdit,endEdit,cancelEdit andediting. Successful edits and source notifications automatically preserve expanded groupswhen the row view is rebuilt. If an edit moves a row to a new group, that groupis not opened implicitly. See saving and restoring expansionfor getExpansionState() and setExpansionState(). Finish or cancel editing before changing data, query or column options. setOptionsrejects those changes while a cell edit is active instead of silently losing itsdraft. Source changed notifications are deferred until the edit ends. Scrollingan edited row out of the rendered viewport attempts confirmation; rejected inputis retained without forcing the cell back into view. Disposing the grid releases its editorand subscriptions but cannot cancel a source update already in flight.
Validation and rejected input

sections.title: Asynchronous source and validation
sections.text: Asynchronous source and validation This example simulates a remote source. Change the quantity and confirm; the editoris unavailable during the request. Quantities above 100 are rejected by the source.The editor closes after the request finishes, and rejected input remains markedin its cell for correction. The source implements filtering, sorting, paging, grouping, group/total summaries,field projection and cancellation checks. It also provides identity, changenotifications, updates, new-row sessions and deletion. ArrayDataSource andLocalGroupingDataSource simulate server-side processing; a real implementationsends these requests to its backend. Total summaries cover the complete filteredresult before paging, and are returned only when requested. The footer belowstarts with a quantity sum of 7 and refreshes after accepted mutations.Hierarchy and undo history are optional capabilities and are not advertised bythis flat, immediately saved source. resolveText replaces the standardtext resolver, without mutating the row. A custom lookup resolver may accept freetext instead of requiring one match. validatechecks both typed and selected values and may be asynchronous. required rejectsnull, undefined and empty strings. Source fieldErrors for the edited field takeprecedence over a general mutation error. Rejected input and its message remainvisible in the cell after editing ends.

sections.title: Rejected input
sections.text: Rejected input Parsing, validation and source failures do not trap focus in an editor. Enter,Tab, pointer navigation and blur finish editing after any pending request settles.The cell displays the rejected input with an error icon and red frame; its tooltipcontains the error message. Reopening the cell restores that input and error.Escape discards the active cell’s rejected input and error, closes its editor ifopen, and displays the source value. This priority also applies with no editoropen, and to pending rows: the first Escape restores the cell, not the whole row.If the active cell has no rejected input/error and belongs to a pending session,Escape cancels that entire session, even when another cell in the row has an error.A second Escape after restoring an invalid pending cell therefore cancels its row.In an existing row, Escape without an error only discards any current cell edit.An open picker still handles Escape first; in-flight saves cannot be interrupted.A successful retry clears the draft, including restoring the source’s current value. Drafts retain only text and an error, never a second typed row value. Text editorsrestore that raw text in their input. Checkbox and switch editors instead showthe source’s accepted boolean value; their error tooltip includes the rejectedtext (for example, Input: "something"). Merely focusing or leaving such a controldoes not clear the draft. Explicitly changing it submits a new boolean value.Custom non-text editors use the field’s formatValue, or string conversion, todescribe rejected actions; provide a matching resolveText for clipboard input. Drafts belong to the grid, keyed by source row identity and field. Supply stablegetRowId values when queries return newrow objects. Without it, row object identity is used. Drafts are not sent to thesource: filtering, sorting, grouping and summaries use only accepted values.hasValidationErrors reportsoutstanding cell or pending-row errors. It is separate from editing.

Cell editing Set allowEdit to true and supply asource with update. Plain arrays are wrappedin an editable ArrayDataSource. A field markedreadonly and synthetic rows such as group headers cannot be edited. Real treerows can be edited when their source supports updates. Double-click or select a cell and press Enter or F2 to edit its existing value;arrows then retain their normal caret/value behavior. Typing a printable characterinstead begins replacement entry, passing that character as the initial text.In replacement entry, arrows confirm and move to the adjacent cell. Clickinginside the editor switches to caret/value navigation. An open picker always ownsits arrow keys. Enter confirms and moves down; Tab confirms and moves across,without opening an editor in the destination cell. Shift reversesthe direction. Escape discards the unaccepted draft. A picker owns its navigationkeys while open, and its Escape closes the picker first. Editing a cell inside an existing selected block preserves the block. After anedit, Tab traverses it row by row and Enter column by column, wrappingat its edges; Shift reverses the direction. With a single selected cell, navigationcontinues across the grid instead. Grid arrow keys collapse the selection (Shiftextends it). Shift+Enter outside editing moves upwards. Avalidation failure or cancellation does not change the selected block.

sections.title: Array and lookup
sections.text: Array and lookup Try text, positive numeric values, a multi-column product lookup, a date and acheckbox. A successful change updates the array and re-queries the grid, includingits summaries. Selecting a picker value or toggling a checkbox confirms that cell. The Add row button creates a source session through the grid. The list below thetable shows each pending session’s ID and offers Insert/Cancel for that specificsession, including rows which are not last. Try pasting invalid quantities intoseveral new rows: Insert keeps an invalid row pending; Cancel removes only itssession. The row header’s context menu also offers Cancel new row. The field’s dataType selects a standard editor. lookuptakes precedence; createEditorcan override either choice. The reusable createFieldEditoradapter can also be used by a form or card view. The host owns each editor anddisposes it when editing ends, including when rejected input is retained in thecell; shared lookup providers outlive the UI. For example, use a switch instead of the standard checkbox, or a time editor fora canonical time string: See ToggleEditor,TimeEditor, andFieldEditorContext. Custom factories mustpass the supplied onCommit; it includes field validation and source-controlledacceptance. getText overrides the cell label;otherwise lookup fields use lookup.getValueText, and other fields useformatValue or standard string conversion. formatValue also supplies text forediting; it can differ from a decorated cell label such as a currency amount.If the editable format differs from the editor’s standard input syntax, providea matching resolveText so formatted values can be parsed back without loss. Lookup items are arbitrary objects. getItemValue chooses the stored value,getItemText chooses its label, and optional columns describe multiple popupcolumns. Without columns, a single label column is supplied automatically.loadItems(query, context) receives search, paging and cancellation options alongwith the original row. Cache data in the shared provider, not the editor instance.

sections.title: Controlling the edit
sections.text: Controlling the edit See Keyboard navigation for completeread-only and editing behavior, including cancellation and redirection throughcellNavigating.

sections.title: Cell picker buttons
sections.text: Cell picker buttons Lookup, date and date-time columns show a cell-owned picker button on mouse hover.Clicking it starts editing and opens the picker in one action, including in thenew-row placeholder. A plain cell click still selects; double-click still edits.Buttons do not create editors until activated and do not shift the cell text. Set editorButtonVisibilityon a column, or through defaultColumnOptions for the grid: Column settings override the default. Read-only cells and group/summary rows haveno picker button. Alt+ArrowDown opens the active cell’s picker without requiringhover. Use the Editor button visibility selector in the first demo to compare.For a custom createEditor returning a PopoverEditor, supply field metadatasuch as editorButton: { icon: "ri-time-line", label: "Open time picker" }.

Filtering The filter option uses a serializable expression that can be evaluated by alocal data source or forwarded to a server. Enable showFilterRow when thegrid should expose a filtering surface. The filter row provides a quick text editor for every data column. Text columnsuse contains by default; number and other typed columns use equality. PressEnter or leave the input to apply the value. The filter button in the rowheader opens the full FilterEditor, where compound AND/OR expressions canbe reviewed and edited in one place. Number and date/datetime columns also support ranges. Use 1..100 for a closedrange, 500.. for values greater than or equal to 500, or ..500 for valuesless than or equal to 500. Date ranges use the same syntax, for exampletoday.. and ..10.12.26. The example starts with an explicit contains filter. Application code canchange it at any time:

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataFilter,DataGridOptions, andFilterFunctionRegistry.
Expansion and restoring state Use the buttons and Grouping context menu in the grouping demo to try these commands.

sections.title: Expand and collapse groups
sections.text: Expand and collapse groups Right-click a column header or its chip in the group panel and open Grouping.The submenu contains Group by … / Ungroup … and Interval for built-inand custom intervals. Grouped fields also offer these commands: Expand to this level opens every group at this level and every parent level.Deeper levels retain their expansion state; previously collapsed descendantsstay collapsed, and previously expanded descendants become visible again. Collapse this level closes groups at this level without changing parentor descendant expansion states. It does not load additional group metadata. For Region → Product, expanding to Product opens both levels. CollapsingProduct leaves regions open and shows their collapsed product groups. Thesecommands affect all groups at the chosen level, not a single group value.Expansion uses one metadata request and one structural update, not a sequenceof per-level commands. Both actions finish active row editing first and use thesame failure/cancellation handling as the API methods below. The commands are available by default, only for grouped fields in non-tree mode.If standardContextMenuItems is an explicit list, include "expandGroupsToLevel"and/or "collapseGroupsAtLevel" to enable them. "groupColumn" controls thegroup/ungroup and interval commands. Grouping is omitted when none of itscommands is available; sorting and Summary remain outside this submenu. SeeGridStandardContextMenuItem. Use Expand all and Collapse all in the demo. The product-level buttonexpands level 1 without opening a collapsed region; open a region to reveal itsretained child state. The optional index is zero-based in groupColumns, not a row index. Invalidindices reject. These methods affect grouping, not hierarchical/tree data.They finish an active edit first; failed validation or an unfinished edit preventsthe operation. Loading errors reject without publishing a partially expanded tree.Changing the data view or disposing the grid cancels outstanding work. Expand-all requests complete nested group metadata through the source’s ordinaryloadData() contract and updates visible indices once. It does not fetch all leafdata rows; normal viewport paging still loads only rows needed for rendering.Collapse-all changes known expansion states without loading group metadata. API: expandAllGroups(),collapseAllGroups().

sections.title: Saving and restoring expansion
sections.text: Saving and restoring expansion getExpansionState() returns an independent GridExpansionStatesnapshot with an expandedGroupKeys array. Keys are opaque: retain them as returnedinstead of constructing or decoding them. The snapshot contains no nodes, rows orquery caches and can be serialized as JSON. Try Save expansion, change the groups’ expansion, then Restore expansionin the demo. Setting a state replaces the current state, rather than merging it.Missing groups are ignored. Expanded descendants below a collapsed parent areretained without implicitly opening that parent; reopening it reveals their state.Both returned and submitted snapshots are copied, so later array changes cannotaffect the grid or an in-flight restore. Restoration uses the same complete grouped-metadata loadData() request asexpand-all. Data rows remain viewport-paged. The old expansion remains in placeuntil metadata loading and validation succeed; failed restoration rejects and isretryable. Replacing the view or disposing the grid cancels outstanding restores.An active row edit must finish successfully first. Reuse a snapshot only with the same source and grouping fields, order andintervals. The snapshot does not identify its source or validate compatibility.Tree-mode expansion is not included: its snapshot is empty, and applying anonempty group snapshot to a tree or ungrouped view rejects. After successful editing, insertion, deletion or source change notifications(including DataTable undo/redo), the grid automatically transfers expansion tothe replacement row view. Existing groups stay in their saved state; groupscreated by a changed field value are not opened automatically. Missing groupsare dropped after restoration. Explicit query/source/grouping changes resetexpansion; use these methods explicitly if you want a compatible state restored.This snapshot does not preserve selection or scroll position. API: getExpansionState(),setExpansionState().

Grouping Grouping turns a flat result into an expandable hierarchy. ConfiguregroupColumns for the initial state, then let users add, remove, and reordergroups from the group panel or column context menu. Dates and numbers can use built-in intervals. Application-specific buckets canbe registered with groupIntervals; each interval defines its own getGroupValue. For example, group amounts into named size buckets: getGroupValue belongs to the interval definition, not the field. The query sends{ field: "amount", interval: "amountSize" }, so a remote source can implementthe same buckets without receiving a JavaScript callback.
