sections.text: Related topics Expansion and restoring state Queries, grouping and summaries

sections.title: Loading groups
sections.text: Loading groups Expanding a group loads its children before publishing the expanded state.If loading fails, the group stays collapsed and can be retried. Concurrentrequests for the same page share one request. Changing the filter, sorting orgrouping replaces the row view and cancels its outstanding queries; disposingthe grid cancels them too. Late responses cannot restore the obsolete view. Custom remote sources should pass QueryArgs.abortSignal to their transport: An individual viewport waiter can stop waiting without cancelling a page stillneeded by another caller. See QueryArgs for thesource query contract.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGrid,GroupInterval, andGroupIntervalDefinition.

Keyboard navigation The active cell identifies the current row and column. Selection ranges describethe highlighted cells; a selected block can remain highlighted while its activecell moves. Click a data cell to focus the grid before using its keyboard commands.See Selection for pointer and selection modes,and Cell editing for editable-source examples.

sections.title: Read-only navigation
sections.text: Read-only navigation With allowEdit: false (the default), navigation never creates a value editor. Key Behavior Arrow keys Move to the adjacent cell and replace the current cell selection. Shift + arrow Extend the selection from its anchor in multiple-cell mode. Page Up / Page Down Move the active cell one visible page up or down in the same column. Home / End Move to the first or last cell in the current row. Ctrl+Home / Ctrl+End (Command on Mac) Move to the first or last selectable cell in the grid. Shift + Page/Home/End Extend the current selection to the destination. Tab / Shift+Tab Move right / left, continuing on the next / previous row. Enter / Shift+Enter Move down / up in the current column. Ctrl+C / Command+C Copy the selected data cells. For a selected multi-cell rectangle, Tab traverses its cells row by row and Entercolumn by column. Traversal wraps inside that rectangle and preserves it; Shiftreverses direction. With multiple separate ranges, traversal uses the last range.With a single selected cell, traversal continues across the grid instead, stoppingat the available boundary. Normal arrows collapse a block; Shift+arrows extend it. In single-row mode, selection remains a single whole row, while the active columncan still move horizontally. In multiple-rows mode, Shift+Up/Down extends thewhole-row selection. Shift+Left/Right does not extend a row range. Enter and Tabuse across-grid navigation in both row modes rather than rectangular traversal.Rows excluded by the grid’s selection rules are skipped during vertical and page movement.

sections.title: Entering edit mode
sections.text: Entering edit mode Editing requires allowEdit, awritable field and a source implementing update. Start action Initial text Arrow behavior Enter or F2 Existing editable text, selected for replacement Controlled by the editor. Double-click Existing editable text, selected for replacement Controlled by the editor. Alt+ArrowDown or cell picker button Existing value, with the picker opened Controlled by the picker while open. Printable character That character replaces the existing text Confirm and move to the adjacent cell. Typing while the editor’s initial row is loading is retained. Clicking inside aneditor that was started by typing switches it to normal caret/value navigation.For example, text arrows move the caret; the number editor can use Up/Down to stepthe value. An open picker always owns its navigation keys, regardless of how thecell edit started. Ctrl/Command/Alt-modified arrows are not used to confirm a typedreplacement entry. Alt+ArrowDown is available for picker fields even wheneditorButtonVisibilityis never. Cell buttons use the same opening path; always also supports touch,while hover is limited to hover-capable pointers. beginEdit without initial text uses normaleditor navigation; supplying text uses replacement-entry navigation:

sections.title: Confirming and cancelling
sections.text: Confirming and cancelling Enter confirms the active edit and moves down. Tab confirms and moves across;Shift reverses direction. Navigation within a selected block follows the sametraversal as read-only mode. The destination cell is not opened for editing.Press Enter again to edit it. Outside editing, Shift+Enter navigates upwards;unmodified Enter starts editing when editing is enabled. Escape first discards any invalid input/error on the active cell and restoresits source value, whether the editor is open or closed. It keeps a pending rowalive in this case. If the cell has no error and belongs to a pending row, Escapecancels that entire row. In an existing row, it discards only the current edit.With an open picker, the first Escape closes/cancels the picker; the next Escapeuses this cell/row priority. Selecting a picker item or changing a checkbox confirmsthat value without requesting a move to another cell. Button-based editors retaintheir native Enter activation. Parsing, validation and source updates may be asynchronous. Movement waits forconfirmation to finish, but does not require success. A failed confirmation closesthe editor and retains the rejected input and error in the cell; reopening itrestores the input. Selection blocks remain intact while the active cell moves.The editor is unavailable while saving; a requestalready in flight cannot be cancelled with Escape. Losing focus attempts toconfirm the edit but does not request keyboard navigation.

sections.title: Customizing navigation
sections.text: Customizing navigation When the source supports new rows, the final * row is an input placeholder.Selecting it creates nothing; starting an edit initializes a source session beforethe editor opens. Tab traverses its cells. Moving away attempts insertion, as doEnter at its bottom boundary and Tab at its last column. A row with cell errorsis not inserted. Failed rows remain pending outside the query, without blockingnavigation or another new-row session. Escape uses the same priority inside andoutside cell editing: discard active-cell invalid input first; otherwise cancelits pending row. Errors in other cells do not change this priority. SeeAdding rows for the lifecycle andexplicit insert/cancel methods. Subscribe to cellNavigating to inspectthe calculated destination before the grid applies it. The synchronousDataGridCellNavigatingEvent containskey, shiftKey, currentCell, mutable targetCell, and cancel.It also exposes ctrlKey and metaKey, so handlers can distinguish row-localHome/End from grid-wide navigation.Coordinates are zero-based visible row and data-column indices, excluding the rowheader. No row data needs to be loaded by a handler merely to inspect coordinates. Prevent Enter from moving after a successful edit: Cancellation preserves both the active cell and the selection. It does not undothe value or remove rejected input: the editor has already closed.The grid still handles the key, so cancelling Tab does not transfer browser focus. Redirect Tab from a particular column to another column in the same row: Choose indices that exist in your visible columns. An invalid, out-of-bounds ornon-selectable destination cancels movement. Redirecting inside an existingselected range retains it; redirecting outside it selects the destination accordingto selectionMode. The event applies to grid-handled arrows, Page Up/Down, Home/End, Enter and Tab,including moves after an edit completes with a validation error. It does not fire for Enterthat starts editing, editor-owned keys, pointer/programmatic selection, pickeracceptance or Escape.It can fire at a boundary even when the proposed cell equals the current cell.Handlers must update the event synchronously; asynchronous subscriptions are notawaited. Prefer changing targetCell over directly changing selection in a handler.Subscriptions are also released when the grid is disposed.

DataGrid DataGrid is a virtualized table component for working with large data sets.It supports configurable columns, grouped rows, summaries, selection, contextmenus, and data sources that can load or query rows on demand.

sections.title: Tabular data
sections.text: Tabular data The demo below uses an ArrayDataSource with 100,000 generated orders. It startswithout grouping or sorting. Click a column header to sort, or drag a columninto the group panel to group the rows. Quantity and Total amount are summedin the total footer across the complete filtered result, and within each groupwhen grouping is applied. Quantity uses displayFormat: "N0", Unit price uses "N2", and Total amountuses "C2€", inheriting the grid’s locale: "bg-BG": thousands are separated, decimalsuse a comma, and euro amounts have two fraction digits. Group summaries andthe total footer reuse these formats. IDs remain unformatted. SeeNumbers, dates and formatting for the supported patterns. The demo uses columnWidthMode: "fixed": columns do not stretch to fill sparespace, and manual resizing changes only the chosen column (independent bydefault in this mode). Horizontal scrolling keeps additional columns accessible. The minimal configuration specifies a data source and columns:

sections.title: Hierarchical data
sections.text: Hierarchical data For parent/child data, configure the ArrayDataSource with its parentField.The dedicated tree data topic demonstrates afile-system style hierarchy.

sections.title: Explore DataGrid features
sections.text: Explore DataGrid features Scrollbars default to scrollbarMode: "thin": a thin thumb stays visible and expandswithin scrollbarHoverDistance (default 50px) of its edge or while dragging,but stays thin during scrolling.Use "auto" to hide them at rest or "always" for fullwidth. The Scroll Engine demo compares all three modes. Continue with the focused topics: Columns and layout Sorting Filtering Grouping Summaries Selection Cell editing Data sources Custom cell rendering Context menus Virtualization and performance

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See the DataGrid API reference,DataGridOptions,ArrayDataSource,DataSource, andSummaryDefinition.

Virtualization and performance DataGrid virtualizes its body and requests only the rows needed for theviewport. This keeps the DOM small even when the logical dataset contains manyrecords. Use a DataSource for paging or remote loading, keep custom renderers focused,and avoid recreating expensive objects during every cell render. The grid alsosupports abortable data requests through the source query contract.

sections.title: Rendering is not query processing
sections.text: Rendering is not query processing Virtualization bounds DOM work; it does not make a full local sort, group oraggregate free. For large remote data, implement paging and grouped metadata inthe source rather than relying on a complete flat-data fallback. Expanding allgroups loads metadata, not every rendered leaf row. For in-memory sources, reuse the source and its query caches across viewportrequests. Use mutation methods or explicit cache invalidation after externalchanges. Keep value accessors pure and avoid expensive allocations inside cellrenderers. Stable VNode keys preserve content identity when cells are patched. See queries and grouping,local processing and cache invalidation, andexpansion behavior.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGrid, DataSource,and VirtualList.

Selection DataGrid supports cell and range selection. Drag across cells to select arectangle, use the row header for whole-row selection, and use the context menuto copy the result. See Keyboard navigation for the fullkey reference, editing behavior and customizable navigation destinations.

sections.title: Selection modes
sections.text: Selection modes Set selectionMode to single-row, multiple-rows or multiple-cells (the default).The same restrictions apply to pointer gestures, keyboard navigation and allprogrammatic range operations on the grid’s SelectionManager. In single-row, clicking, dragging, adding or extending a range replaces selectionwith one whole row, including with Ctrl/Cmd or Shift. In multiple-rows, Ctrl/Cmdadds disjoint whole-row ranges and Shift or dragging extends the latest range.Normal arrow navigation replaces selection; Shift+Up/Down extends or shrinks arow range. Left/Right keep active column navigation but never create partial-rowselection. Tab moves between columns and wraps to the next row; Enter movesvertically. Tab/Enter replace row-mode selection with the destination row. Changing modes normalizes existing ranges. multiple-rows expands cell rectanglesto whole-row ranges; single-row keeps only the active row. Returning to cell moderetains whole-row ranges until a new selection gesture. The active cell remainsindependent of the ranges: setActiveCell() alone changes focus coordinates withoutselecting a row. Direct manager mutations require grid.refresh() to update visuals. Selection state is rendered by the grid cell, so custom renderers do not needto know how selection colors or edge borders work. Applications can inspect orclear the current state with getSelectedRanges(), getActiveSelectionCell(),and clearSelection().

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See SelectionManager,CellSelectionState, andDataGrid.

Sorting Sorting can be changed from the column context menu or configured withorderBy. Use a string for ascending order or a tuple for an explicitdirection. The example starts with a two-column sort. Try the following interactions: Click a column header to cycle through ascending, descending, and clear. Thisbehavior is enabled by sortOnHeaderClick (true by default). Hold Shift while clicking a header to add the column to the current sort orupdate only that column. The other sort columns and their priorities remainunchanged. Open a column’s context menu and choose Sort Ascending, Sort Descending,or Clear sorting. Clear sorting is not shown for grouped columns becausea grouped column must remain sorted. Holding Shift while choosing an actionapplies it only to the current column; without Shift, the selected columnbecomes the only sort criterion. Dragging a header still reorders the column and does not trigger sorting. Whenmultiple columns are sorted, each header shows its sort priority.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See DataGridOptions andDataGrid.

Summaries Summaries add useful aggregate values to grouped data and to the completeresult set. Built-in types include count, sum, avg, min, max, anddistinct. Custom summaries can maintain their own accumulator state. The group and total summaries are independent settings. A group summary iscalculated for each group, while a total summary is calculated for the completefiltered result, even when the grid is grouped or paged. The context menu keepsboth settings in sync when a summary is selected there, but they can still beconfigured differently in code when that is useful. The demo shows both cases. The first grid uses sum for both levels, so thefooter can display the value without a label. The second grid uses sum forgroups and avg for the total. In that case the footer includes avg: so themeaning of the value is explicit.

sections.title: Configure summaries
sections.text: Configure summaries

sections.title: Remote data sources
sections.text: Remote data sources Set a numeric column’s displayFormat (for example N0, N2 or C2€) andoptional locale to format both group and total summaries consistentlywith its data cells. Raw aggregate results remain numeric; the source does notformat them. Counts (count and distinct) stay plain counts, even on currencyor percentage columns. Row-dependent getText/lookup/formatValue callbacksare not used for summaries. See Formatting. The source computes totals across the complete filtered result, before paging. See Queries, grouping and summaries for the shared request/response contract.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See SummaryDefinition,SummaryContext, andSummaryType.
Tree data A DataGrid can display hierarchical rows when its data source identifies theparent of each row. This is useful for file systems, organizational charts,categories, and other nested data.

sections.title: Parent and child rows
sections.text: Parent and child rows The demo uses parentField: "parentId". Root rows have a null parent and childrows refer to their parent by id. See the DataGrid API reference,ArrayDataSource, andDataSource.
Date editor DateEditor combines a text input with the standalone DatePicker.It uses the same validation and asynchronous acceptance contract as otherValue editors, with no dependency on data sources.

sections.title: Delivery and booking dates
sections.text: Delivery and booking dates Type a date and press Enter, or use the calendar button. Delivery uses ISO text;booking uses dd.MM.yyyy, while both keep ISO values. The booking editorrestricts dates to October–November 2026 and rejects weekends. Enable the simulatedsave failure to see how a selected date remains available for correction or retry.Empty text resolves to null; the booking example adds a required-field validator.

sections.title: Configure an editor
sections.text: Configure an editor The value is a strict date-only YYYY-MM-DD string or null. No timezone isadded and no timestamp conversion is performed. locale affects DatePicker labelsand the standard dateFormat: "d"; explicit patterns are independent of locale.min and max are inclusive and applyto typed values, calendar choices, external resolution and setValue().

sections.title: Input, picker and focus
sections.text: Input, picker and focus Enter confirms text; Escape restores the last confirmed value. Leaving thecompound editor also confirms by default; set commitOnBlur: false to defer it.Moving focus into DatePicker does not confirm pending input. openOnFocus: true opens and focuses the calendar when the input receives focus.Arrow keys navigate dates and Enter chooses the focused date. The default isfalse, shared with LookupEditor; lookup keeps focus in its search input instead.Returning to the input after choosing a date or pressing Escape does not reopen it.Press Escape to return to direct text editing. The booking example enables this option. The inset calendar button or Alt+Down opens DatePicker and focuses the selected day.The button does not add a Tab stop: Tab reaches the input directly. Arrow keys inside the text inputremain native caret operations. Opening the picker browses the typed date whenvalid, without saving it; invalid text still permits choosing a replacement.DatePicker navigation does not change the editor value. Choosing a day or Todayupdates the input and closes the picker immediately, then starts validation andconfirmation. During asynchronous acceptance, the input and trigger are unavailablefor another edit. A failure appears on the editor without reopening the picker. Escape in month/year choices first returns to days. Escape from the day viewcloses the picker, restores confirmed text and returns focus to the input.Ordinary outside dismissal closes the panel without discarding pending text.A failed validation or save keeps the draft and error in the compact validation indicator; correct the value, retrycommit(), or call cancel().

sections.title: Resolve and format text
sections.text: Resolve and format text Set dateFormat: "dd.MM.yyyy" for matching display and parsing; the default is "yyyy-MM-dd". dateFormat: "d" uses the locale short-date layout. Values remain canonical YYYY-MM-DD strings or null. See Dates, times and formatting for supported tokens, custom conversion precedence and strict parsing. resolveText() converts without validation or saving; calendar bounds still apply.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference DateEditor,DateEditorOptions,TextEditor, DatePicker.

DatePicker DatePicker is a standalone date picker, suitable for a form, panel or editor popup.It uses the standard UI styles, inherits theme colors and does not depend on adata source or perform any save operation. DatePicker selects a date; it is not an event or scheduling calendar. UseDateEditor for a text input with DatePicker in a popover. The view is described with keyed v() nodes. Dates, weeks and toolbar controlsretain their DOM identity when patched. Initial rendering is immediate; subsequentchanges use the Elgora UI scheduler and are batched on the next animation frame.State and selection notifications update immediately, before that visual patch.Explicit keyboard navigation focuses its target after patching; ordinary updatesdo not replace retained buttons or restore focus unnecessarily.

sections.title: Pick a date
sections.text: Pick a date The selected date uses primary color; today’s date has a subtle border. Muteddates belong to adjacent months and remain selectable unless excluded by bounds.Change the locale or first weekday, and try the optional booking-date restriction.

sections.title: Date-only values
sections.text: Date-only values Dates use strict YYYY-MM-DD strings, or null for no selection. Invalid datessuch as 2026-02-29 are rejected rather than normalized. A date is not a timestamp:it is not converted to UTC or shifted by a time zone. UTC-based arithmetic is usedinternally only to calculate calendar days and format their labels consistently. value is the selected date. Keyboard focus and the displayed month (YYYY-MM)are independent: browsing never selects a date. setValue(date) loads a datesilently; showMonth(date) browses without changing selection. setValue(null)clears selection and displays the current day, clamped to the allowed range. Only explicit user choices invoke onSelect and the selected observable event.Choosing an already selected date still emits a selection notification. A hostsuch as a date editor decides whether that choice should be validated or saved.

sections.title: Navigation
sections.text: Navigation Header arrows browse previous/next months. Click the month title to choose among twelve months. Click the year title to choose among twelve years; arrows browse year blocks. Left/Right move one day; Up/Down move one week. Home/End move to the first/last day of the configured week. PageUp/PageDown move a month, clamping to the last valid day when necessary. Shift+PageUp/PageDown move a year, including leap-day handling. Enter or Space select the focused day. Escape returns from month/year choices to the day view. Today selects the current day and emits selected and onSelect, even when thatdate is already selected. It is disabled when today lies outside the inclusivemin/max bounds; no substitute date is selected. The default day isread from the browser’s local clock. Set today to supply an application dateor make a demonstration reproducible.

sections.title: Bounds and locale
sections.text: Bounds and locale Bounds are inclusive and apply to pointer selection, keyboard navigation andexternal values. Entire months/years outside the range are disabled. Assigning avalue outside the range throws an error; browsing with showMonth() is clamped.Supported years are 0001 through 9999. Locale controls month names, weekday names and accessible full-date labels.The first weekday is explicit: 0 = Sunday through 6 = Saturday, defaulting toMonday. DatePicker includes a six-week grid, one keyboard tab stop for days,selection semantics and accessible labels for each date.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference DatePicker, DatePickerOptions.
FilterEditor FilterEditor edits a structured filter. It is not a ValueEditor and does not save row values. Supply field metadata, then apply its filter to your chosen source.

sections.title: Product filter playground
sections.text: Product filter playground Click a preset, then edit its conditions using FilterEditor and clickApply Filter. The table and readable summary show the applied filter, notunapplied editor changes. Clear removes the filter.Apply Filter is gray when the filter has not changed and primary-colored whilethere are unapplied edits. It remains clickable in either state, allowing thecurrent filter to be applied again. Returning to the applied values makes it gray. Try the numeric expression input with 20..100, 100.. or ..50.It replaces the complete filter with a price condition. Expand Filter JSON andfilter-row expressions to see the structure and the reverse conversion.The displayed evalFilter count is calculated separately from the ArrayDataSourcequery over the same records. FilterEditor currently edits binary conditions and explicit AND/OR groups,including nested groups. It does not provide a NOT node. The NOT preset isevaluated and displayed without loading it into the visual editor.Do not assume that every DataFilter structure can be round-tripped throughFilterEditor. API: FilterEditor,setFilter,FilterEditorOptions.onApply,DataFilter.

HTML editor HtmlEditor provides an editable rich-text surface for content stored as HTML.It follows the shared value-editor lifecycle:the editor keeps a draft, while the host decides when that draft is accepted orpersisted.

sections.title: Edit and accept content
sections.text: Edit and accept content Edit the sample, select text and try the formatting buttons or keyboard shortcuts(Ctrl+B or ⌘B). Save calls commit() and updates the saved HTML shown below;Discard calls cancel() and restores the last accepted content. The examplesimulates an asynchronous save callback. The demo’s buttons call the editor’s command API. Typing, deletion, Enter,Shift+Enter, bold and italic use model transactions. Undo and redo restore both thedocument and selection. The selected-element inspector exposes compact Basiccontrols for the selected element; more advanced structural commands are stillunder development. Dropped content is blocked. Use Sample to switch between rich text, layout containers with media, and atable. Changing the sample replaces the current draft. Try Enter in the middleof a card or cell, Backspace/Delete at a paragraph boundary, then Undo and Redo.Place the caret in text and use Insert HTML to try an inline fragment, list,table or layout card. This uses the same insertion command as HTML paste. The editor creates and owns the toolbar above the surface and the inspector onthe right because the demo enables toolbar: true and inspector: true.Both options default to false, preserving the compact editor. They are constructionoptions; this first scaffold does not provide runtime visibility toggles. The toolbar runs the existing Bold, Italic, Undo and Redo commands, with disabledstates and arrow-key navigation. The inspector’s selector opens a virtualizedTreeView showing tags and shortened descriptions. Itfollows the text caret; choosing a tree item previews an inspection target withoutchanging the remembered caret, document or history. Properties contains compactBasic commands such as Bold, Italic, block type, text color, text size and alignment.Commands with choices use one shared Lookup editor and commit through the same modeltransaction and Undo/Redo history as the editing surface. Advanced remains theplace for direct classes, attributes and styles in a later step.On narrow screens this first layout stacks the inspector below the surface;a responsive drawer and resizable panel are future work. For a non-collapsed range, the selector displays Mixed when selected contentbelongs to multiple text/atomic elements. Enclosing shells alone do not make asingle text owner mixed. The tree uses the same interval coverage as Copy/Delete:fully and partially covered nodes share the same blue background. A circularindicator after the tag shows coverage: empty for unselected, half-filled forpartial, filled for full, with a localized tooltip. These are decorative statusindicators, not checkboxes. A right-arrow icon (tooltip: “Keyboard focus”) in a fixed gutter at the start of the focused row, before indentation and the disclosure chevron, replacesthe dotted focus outline in this HTML tree only; the tree viewport retains itsfocus frame. Empty elements and images count only when their own interval is covered.Opening the tree reveals partial endpoint containers; fully selected subtrees canremain collapsed and show their coverage on the parent. Their descendants receivethe same marks when expanded. A caret alone has no range-coverage marks. Coverage is separate from the tree’s keyboard focus and single inspection-previewchoice. Choosing a preview may replace the Mixed label until the next text-selectionchange, but never changes the range or its highlights. Coverage is also announcedin the accessible row labels. Only this HTML tree uses a monospace font, gray tagbadges and muted descriptions; the selector uses the same label rendering in atransparent, borderless-looking ghost button, with standard hover and keyboard-focusfeedback. Ordinary TreeView appearance is unchanged. The breadcrumb above the selector lists only the three nearest parents, notthe current element (already shown in the selector). A leading … opens earlierancestors in document order. Every ancestor can be previewed without moving thetext selection or adding an undo entry; keyboard activation uses native buttons,and Escape closes the overflow popup and returns focus to its trigger.For Mixed, the path includes the nearest common ancestor of the selectedcontent owners. If no authored element contains the whole range, the path is hidden:the virtual document root is not shown as an invented body element. Root-levelinspection targets also have no parent breadcrumb. The path remains single-line.

sections.title: Surface and orchestration
sections.text: Surface and orchestration HtmlEditorSurface is a standalone Component. It owns the contenteditable area,model, DOM mapping, text selection, input handling and the single Undo/Redo history.It does not have value, confirmedValue, commit() or cancel(). HtmlEditor remains a ValueEditor<string>. It creates and disposes one surfaceand the optional HtmlEditorToolbar/HtmlEditorInspector, connects their events,and owns parsing/validation/external acceptance through the value-editor lifecycle.The existing content, document, selection, execute, canUndo and canRedoAPI delegates to that same surface; no second model or history is maintained.Use editor.setHtml() for an accepted baseline, not editor.surface.setHtml():the low-level surface method only replaces its document and resets its history. For a custom host that needs only the editing area: The host owns saving and any baseline when using the surface directly. The built-intoolbar and inspector never save content or create their own edit history.

sections.title: Use in a host form
sections.text: Use in a host form html and getHtml() return the editor’s current serialized draft. The documentproperty returns a detached snapshot; changing that object does not change theeditor. setHtml(html) replaces the content and establishes a new acceptedbaseline. Use cancel() to return to that baseline.

sections.title: HTML node model
sections.text: HTML node model The document contains two node types: a text leaf { id, type: "text", text }and an HTML element { id, type: "element", tag, classes, styles, attributes, children }.Images, video and table cells are ordinary elements identified by their tag.Their properties live only in attributes: for example src, alt, rowspanand colspan remain HTML strings. Boolean attributes use presence with an emptystring, such as controls: ""; absence means the attribute is not set. Renderingdoes not add media attributes such as controls or alt automatically. id is the editor’s internal identity. An authored HTML ID such as id="intro"lives in attributes.id. classes stores unique tokens in authored order;class and style are never duplicated inside attributes. styles is an ordered array of { name, value, important? } declarations. Itretains duplicate declarations, shorthand/longhand order, fallback values and!important. Standard names use CSS notation, for example background-color;custom-property names such as --Card-gap are case-sensitive. The model storesauthored inline CSS; computed styles from a stylesheet are not copied into it.Structural editing rules are independent of an element’s CSS display value. These helpers prepare declaration lists without mutating the input array and shareunmodified declarations. Setting a property removes its previous exact-namedeclarations and appends the replacement; other shorthand/longhand declarationsretain their order. Lookup respects priority for the exact property name, butdoes not compute shorthand expansion or stylesheet inheritance. The helpers donot apply property edits to the live editor themselves.

sections.title: Commands and history
sections.text: Commands and history execute() returns false when an operation cannot be applied to the currentselection or the editor is unavailable. Commands use the last editor selection,so a host toolbar can receive focus before invoking them. Bold and italic applyto a selected range across supported sibling text blocks, or change the format of subsequentlytyped text at a collapsed caret. Moving the selection clears that typing override. Supported operations are insertText, insertHtml, deleteBackward,deleteForward, insertParagraph, insertLineBreak, indent, outdent, bold, italic, undoand redo. Commands use shared structural operations for positions, inlineranges, splitting, merging and replacement. Their behavior follows the HTMLelement’s semantics, independently of CSS display.

sections.title: Structural editing rules
sections.text:
Structural editing rules The built-in rules classify supported elements as inline content, text blocks,list containers/items, layout containers, table structure/cells or atomic content.getHtmlEditorElementBehavior(element) returns the read-only built-in behavior(kind and optional splitTag); it does not register custom behaviors. Content Behavior Text and inline wrappers Insertion and replacement preserve surrounding formatting. Equivalent inline boundaries share one logical offset. Paragraphs and headings Enter splits; Backspace/Delete joins compatible siblings at their shared boundary. The right half of a heading becomes a paragraph. Lists Enter splits an item; an empty item exits or moves up one level. A paragraph inside a structured item splits the item and transfers its following content. Containers, including flex/grid Editing stays inside the container. Enter on direct inline content creates paragraphs inside it, preserving the shell and its presentation. Table cells Text, formatting, paragraph splitting and supported HTML paste work inside a cell. Its row/cell identity and attributes remain intact. Images, video, hard breaks and dividers Atomic content is deleted as a unit from the adjacent boundary. Media descendants are not rich-text editing areas. Inline runs beside nested blocks are wrapped in a paragraph when edited. Forexample, editing the direct A in
A

B

C
creates a paragrapharound A and preserves the outer div and the other children. This structuralpreparation belongs to the same undo step as the edit. At a collapsed caret, Backspace/Delete never merge across a table cell or layoutcontainer boundary. An empty flex/grid item retains its container and its finalempty paragraph; an extra empty paragraph can still join the preceding paragraphinside that same item. Figure captions, details summaries and preformatted blocksalso retain their outer boundary. Ordinary paragraph joins ignore ASCII formattingwhitespace between sibling blocks, but do not skip authored nonbreaking spaces.These caret rules do not prevent an explicit range from removing fully selectedelements under the coverage rules below. Within text, Backspace/Delete remove complete graphemes using Intl.Segmenter,including emoji sequences and combining marks split across inline formatting.A restored caret inside a grapheme deletes that entire grapheme. Atomic elementshave their own boundaries: a combining mark after an image cannot cause the imageto be deleted together with the mark. Without Intl.Segmenter, deletion fallsback to Unicode code points, preserving surrogate pairs but not guaranteeingcomplete multi-code-point grapheme deletion. Selected ranges use a shared recursive removal operation, including ranges acrosstable cells, list items and different layout containers. Partially covered elementsretain their shell, identity, attributes and unselected children. Fully coveredelements are removed with their whole subtree, up to the highest fully coveredancestor; the document root itself is never removed. This is different fromBackspace/Delete at a collapsed caret, which still respects structural join barriers. For example, selecting from A|BC in a table cell through DE|F in a list itemand typing X leaves AX in that cell and F in that list item. Fully selectedelements between them disappear. The partial cell and item are not merged. Selectingall content of a table removes the table, not just its text. Images and other atomsparticipate in coverage; selecting text alone does not select an adjacent image.Empty elements also require coverage by the range: they are not automaticallyremoved just because they contain no text. After range deletion, table rows, sections and tables emptied by that operationare removed even if source indentation remains. Pre-existing empty rows, survivingcells, captions and other unselected authored content are retained. The insertionbookmark follows the surviving parent gap when an emptied shell disappears.Ranges can extend from a nested table into an outer cell without merging thosecells. Partially covered merged cells retain their authored rowspan/colspan.Range deletion follows document order; it does not perform rectangular spreadsheetselection or recalculate the spans of surviving cells after structural removal. Replacement inserts at the surviving start position, independent of selectiondirection. If the starting subtree was removed, its former position in the survivingparent becomes the insertion gap. If insertion is not legal there, the editor triespositions after successive enclosing elements. For example, text replacing a removedcell can be placed after the remaining table, while a cell fragment can use the rowgap directly. Removal and insertion form one undo step. Invalid HTML replacementleaves both the document and history unchanged. Unsupported operations return false; commands do not fall through to native browserediting. Dedicated table row/column commands, custom element behavior registrationand drag/drop remain future work.

sections.title: Preformatted text and quotes
sections.text: Preformatted text and quotes Inside one pre area, Enter and Shift+Enter insert literal newline characterswithout splitting the preformatted block. Text input and plain-text paste retainnewlines rather than introducing br elements. Replacing text within that areakeeps its pre shell. Inline code outside pre follows ordinary paragraph rules. Tab indents the current line or selected lines with one tab character; Shift+Tabremoves one leading tab or up to four leading spaces. A selection ending exactlyat the next line’s start excludes that next line. Selection direction and caretpositions follow the indentation edits. indent/outdent are supported onlyinside one preformatted area; elsewhere Tab keeps its normal focus navigation.Each changed command is one undo step; outdenting an unindented line adds nohistory entry. Navigation and IME composition retain their existing behavior. In a blockquote, Enter in an empty final paragraph lifts that paragraph out ofthe quote. Backspace at the beginning of its first direct text block lifts thatblock before the remaining quote. Both operations remove only one quote level,retain formatting and preserve the remaining quoted content. Direct inline quotecontent becomes a paragraph when lifted. These rules do not cross an interveninglayout, list or table-cell boundary. Enter in a nonfinal empty paragraph staysinside the quote; Shift+Enter inserts a hard break without exiting it.

sections.title: List shortcuts and boundaries
sections.text: List shortcuts and boundaries At the end of a paragraph beginning with * , -  or a number followed by . ,Enter converts the paragraph to a list and starts the next item. For example,- First becomes a bullet item followed by an empty item ready for typing.A marker alone creates one empty item. Numbered markers preserve their startingnumber (5. First starts at 5). Conversion preserves inline formatting and is oneundoable command. It does not trigger on Space, Shift+Enter, in the middle of aparagraph, inside code/preformatted content or inside an existing list. In a nonempty list item, Enter splits the item. In an empty item, Enter exits thelist into a paragraph; in a nested list it lifts the item one level instead.Following items are preserved in a trailing list when necessary. These changesand their caret positions participate in Undo/Redo just like other commands.Backspace in an empty list item removes it and returns the caret to the end ofthe preceding item. For the first item it exits the list, or lifts it one levelwhen nested. Empty inline wrappers, paragraphs and a single break are supported.Backspace at the first editable position of the first nonempty item also exitsthe list, or lifts the item one level when nested. Inline content becomes aparagraph; a structured item retains its content in a flow container. Formatting,authored presentation and following items are retained. On a nested lift, followingnested items and content after the nested list move with the lifted item. A laterparagraph inside the same item joins locally instead of exiting the list; a tableor layout boundary is not crossed. Ordered lists retain the remaining numbering,including reversed lists and HTML with whitespace between items.Backspace at the beginning of a paragraph immediately following a list joins itscontent to the final editable list item, preserving inline formatting. The caretstays at the join point; Undo restores the separate paragraph and its selection.Backspace at the start of a structured list item and Delete at the preceding item’send share the same boundary operation. Only the touching text blocks merge; followingparagraphs and nested lists are preserved. A table or layout shell at that boundaryis not implicitly entered or merged. The editor intercepts supported cancelable beforeinput operations and appliesthe resulting model and selection to the DOM. keydown handles Ctrl/⌘+B,Ctrl/⌘+I, Ctrl/⌘+Z, Ctrl/⌘+Shift+Z and Ctrl+Y. Events continue bubbling.All cancelable non-composition input is prevented, including unknown input typesand commands that cannot be applied at the current selection. There is no generalbrowser-editing fallback. Consequently, operations such as native underline or worddeletion are blocked until dedicated commands support them. Plain caret movementand mouse/touch text selection remain native and synchronize the remembered selection. IME is allowed to update its composition DOM without rerendering, then reconciledafter composition and its final input have finished. Noncancelable beforeinputalso permits a bounded native edit, read back through the parser and normalizationinto one undoable transaction. Permission is consumed by input or settled at thenext task boundary; it does not authorize unrelated future input. A task ratherthan a microtask lets browser default actions finish before reconciliation. On platforms thatomit compositionstart, a composing beforeinput uses this bounded path. History retains up to 100 document/selection snapshots, with one entry per changedcommand or permitted native transaction. canUndo and canRedo expose availability.Typing is not yet coalesced into word-sized undo groups. setHtml(), cancellationand a successful modified commit start a new history scope. Returning to theinitial document with undo also clears modified.

sections.title: HTML fragment insertion and clipboard
sections.text: HTML fragment insertion and clipboard insertHtml and clipboard paste share the same placement rules. The fragment isparsed inertly through the supported tag, attribute and presentation policy.Scripts, embedded documents, event attributes and unsafe URL schemes are removed.An empty/fully removed fragment is rejected without deleting the selection. Inline content is inserted inside the current text block. A single unstyledparagraph is treated as its inline content; authored block attributes, classesand styles keep a paragraph structural instead. Lists, tables and layout containers split the current text block. Text on bothsides and its inline formatting are preserved. Editable content after theinserted structure receives the caret so typing can continue outside it. A cell, list item or layout container retains its outer shell. Block contentstays inside that shell; a list pasted inside an item becomes a nested list. At an explicit list gap, content is adapted to list items. At a table row gap,cell fragments are accepted, while paragraphs are rejected. Standalone listitems, rows and cells at flow positions receive the necessary list/table wrappers.After insertion at a table structural gap, the caret moves to the end of thelast inserted editable cell so typing can continue. If the fragment containsno editable area (for example, columns only), it moves after the enclosing table. Selected ranges can cross cells and containers in either direction. Recursiveremoval preserves partial shells and removes fully covered subtrees, then insertsat the surviving start or the nearest legal outer gap as described above. Every inserted node receives a fresh editor identity. Conflicting authored HTMLIDs are given unique suffixes, and fragment-local href="#..." and supported ARIAID references follow the new IDs. Insertion is one Undo/Redo step including theselection. This policy supports the editor’s HTML subset, not arbitrary scripts,stylesheets, custom elements or every malformed HTML nesting. If HTML placement fails, the paste handler tries nonempty text/plain content;an empty text fallback never clears the selection. Plain-text-only paste insertsline breaks inside the current editing area. This editing policy does not replacean application’s server-side HTML sanitization. Copy and Cut intercept the native clipboard events and export from the model,not from the browser’s serialization of the live DOM. Both text/html andtext/plain are written. Runtime node attributes and view-only placeholders arenever included. Export requires a live selection inside this editor; a rememberedtoolbar selection is not used when the native selection is outside it. Copy isavailable in read-only mode; Cut requires an editable, settled model. During IMEcomposition or pending native reconciliation neither operation exports stale data. Extraction shares interval coverage with recursive deletion, but does not mutatethe model: fully selected subtrees are cloned, partially selected shells containonly selected descendants, and unselected nodes are omitted. Selection directiondoes not affect output. For a range from A|BC in a table cell through DE|F in alist item, the HTML fragment contains a table/cell shell with BC and a list/itemshell with DE, not the unselected A and F. These wrappers make the fragmentself-contained; the selection is not expanded to whole cells or items. Partial ordered lists adjust start to preserve the original first selected item’snumber, including reversed lists. Partial tables are compact fragments of selectedcells: rowspan and colspan are removed within that partial table rather thanpulling unselected cells into the clipboard. Original grid geometry is not retained.A completely selected table, including complete nested tables, retains its spans.Plain text uses newlines for block/list boundaries and hard breaks, tabs betweentable cells, and image alt text; preformatted text whitespace is preserved. Cut writes both clipboard formats before applying one structural deletion transaction.If clipboard data is unavailable or a write throws, the model, selection and historyare unchanged. A later native deleteByCut is blocked, preventing a second deletion.Undo restores the cut content and directed selection, but does not revert the systemclipboard. Copy itself creates no history entry. Clipboard writes use the synchronousevent data API; no asynchronous clipboard permission request is needed. The editor observes external DOM changes. Unannounced input and external text,structural or attribute mutations are reverted to the model, without modifyingthe draft or undo/redo history. Only explicitly permitted native edits can beadopted. This is an editing policy, not a security boundary against scripts on thesame page. Reconciliation pauses the observer and updates the DOM using the existingVNode renderer. Empty blocks use a view-only line-break filler, omitted from savedHTML.

sections.title: Selection and focus
sections.text: Selection and focus selection returns a detached snapshot of the last selection inside the editor.Each endpoint contains a nodeId and an offset. Text offsets count UTF-16 units;element offsets count supported child nodes. The content root also has its ownidentity, allowing ranges between top-level blocks. nativeSelection exposes thelive browser selection only while both endpoints belong to this editor. selectionChanged emits detached snapshots when the remembered range changes.Moving focus or selecting text outside the editor retains the last editor range.restoreSelection() without an argument restores that remembered range and focusesthe editing surface. Forward and backward ranges retain their direction. Identities survive native input while the same DOM nodes survive. Commands map theirresulting selection to the updated model. Removed endpointsinvalidate the remembered range; offsets are clamped when text becomes shorter.setHtml(), cancellation and a successful modified commit rebuild the content andinvalidate saved identities. Snapshots are local to one editor and document scope;they are not persistent bookmarks across document replacements. Use execute()to edit content; restoring a selection alone does not change the document.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference HtmlEditor,HtmlEditorOptions,HtmlEditorNode,HtmlEditorElement,HtmlEditorText,HtmlEditorStyle,ValueEditor.
Lookup editor LookupEditor<TValue, TItem> stores a value (for example a customer ID) whiledisplaying the selected item’s name. It shares validation and asynchronousacceptance with Value editors.

sections.title: Customer picker
sections.text: Customer picker Click the input or start typing to open the results. Search by customer name orcountry. Try Customer 001 for a unique match and Customer for an ambiguous one.The simulated remote source has 500 items and loads pages on demand. Drag thebottom-right grip to resize the popup; reopening retains its dimensions.

sections.title: Configure value, items and paging
sections.text: Configure value, items and paging loadItems receives search, skip, top and an optional abortSignal.totalCount must describe all matching items before paging. Honor cancellationwhen possible; the editor also ignores obsolete results if the source cannot abort.Search is debounced by searchDelay (150ms by default). pageSize defaults to 50. getValueText resolves the initial or externally supplied value independentlyof result pages. Label responses cannot overwrite newer values or typed searches.

sections.title: Search, choose and cancel
sections.text: Search, choose and cancel Typing or pasting changes search text, not the stored value. The filtered popupuses a virtualized DataGrid in single-row mode, without grouping, editing,context menus or summaries. Headers appear when more than one column is configured.Its columns use columnWidthMode: "stretch-all", filling extra popup width inproportion to their base widths while preserving horizontal scroll in narrow popups. The inset arrow button toggles the popup. Alt+Down opens it without selecting aresult or changing the value. The button does not add a Tab stop; Tab reaches theinput directly, and Left/Right retain native caret behavior. Set openOnFocus: true to also show results when the input receives focus, keepingfocus in the input. This option defaults to false, as in DateEditor. Clicking ortyping in the lookup input still opens results independently of this option. Up/Down focus a result row while keeping native focus in the input. The gridscrolls only when needed to reveal the row, without aligning each row at the top.Enter acceptsthat explicit row; without a focused row it resolves typed text. Clicking a resultalso accepts that item. Escape restores the last accepted value and text.Outside dismissal closes the list while retaining the draft. IME Enter does not confirm. Validation and onCommit run before acceptance. While awaiting them the editor isbusy. The results popup closes when confirmation starts, before asynchronous work finishes. Theeditor keeps the candidate and error available through the validation indicator for a later retry.The editor does not write to a data source itself.

sections.title: Resolve pasted text
sections.text: Resolve pasted text The default resolver requests up to two items and checks totalCount: zero matchesor more than one match throw an error. There is no first-result or exact-textfallback. A single row in a page is not sufficient when the total count is greaterthan one. The host can use this method for tabular paste and separately validateand save the returned value. A custom shared resolveText option may overrideconversion when the application has a dedicated resolver endpoint.

sections.title: Popup size
sections.text: Popup size Without popupWidth, the popup matches the input’s width, with a minimum of200 CSS pixels where the viewport permits. Automatic width is measured each timethe popup opens. An explicit popupWidth overrides this behavior; after a manualresize, the chosen size is retained on reopening instead of matching the input.popupHeight defaults to 300 CSS pixels. All widths are constrained to the viewport.resizable defaults to true. The reusable ResizeHandle constrainsthe size to the viewport, with minimum dimensions of 200×140 where space permits.Size is retained only for the lifetime of this editor, not saved globally.
