sections.text: API reference LookupEditor,LookupEditorOptions,LookupQuery,LookupResult,ResizeHandle.

Lifecycle and resource ownership Component is ElgoraUI’s small, composable abstraction over a nativeHTMLElement. It keeps the browser DOM as the actual rendering target, whileadding the structure and behavior needed to build larger web applications.

sections.title: Component and HTMLElement
sections.text: Component and HTMLElement An HTMLElement gives you a browser node: attributes, properties, events, andchildren. A Component owns an HTMLElement through its dom property andadds a consistent component boundary around it. The most important additions are: Composition — children and append() accept text, numbers, nativenodes, other Components, and nested arrays. Lifecycle — comcreate, commount, comunmount, and comdispose let acomponent initialize, connect, disconnect, and release resources. State — a component can keep local state and create observable valuesthrough com.observable(). Reactive rendering — renderOnChange() reruns a small rendering actionwhen an ObservableValue changes. Bindings — properties, attributes, styles, classes, and UI styles can beconnected to observable values with bindProperty(), bindAttribute(),bindStyle(), bindClass(), and bindUiStyle(). Safe mounting — mount(), unmount(), dispose(), and lock() providepredictable ownership of the DOM tree. The component’s dom remains a normal HTMLElement, so native browser APIscan still be used when needed. Use the Component API for changes to thecomponent tree so lifecycle behavior stays consistent.

sections.title: Component lifecycle
sections.text: Component lifecycle A component has three distinct lifecycle phases. The phase determines whetherthe component is connected to the document and which resources it should own.

sections.title: Create
sections.text: Create The constructor creates the component’s dom, applies its options, appends itsinitial children, and invokes comcreate once. Use this phase for component-owned DOM setup and state initialization. A component does not have to bemounted yet, so code in this phase should not assume that dom.isConnected istrue.

sections.title: Mount and unmount
sections.text: Mount and unmount mount(container) connects the component to an HTMLElement or CSS selector.It invokes lifecycle callbacks for the complete component subtree inparent-to-child order: commount option callback; protected onMount() hook; the same sequence for each child component. unmount() removes the component from its parent without destroying it. Thecomponent remains in memory, keeps its state, and can be mounted again. Itscallbacks run in the reverse order, children first and parent last. The callbacks are not copied from a parent to its children. Every componentreceives its own lifecycle callbacks when the component tree is traversed. Use onMount() and onUnmount() for resources that depend on an externalmount context, such as a listener on window, document, or the host element.Pair every subscription created in onMount() with its removal inonUnmount() so repeated mount/unmount cycles do not create duplicatelisteners. Subscriptions to the component’s own dom can be created duringcreation and remain available while the component is detached. Always call mount() and unmount() instead of directly appending or removingdom; direct DOM operations bypass lifecycle callbacks for the component andits descendants.

sections.title: Dispose
sections.text: Dispose dispose() is the permanent end of the component lifecycle. It unmounts thecomponent, disposes its child components, releases registered resources, andinvokes comdispose. A disposed component cannot be mounted again. Usedispose() for resources owned for the entire lifetime of the component, whileonUnmount() is for resources that only belong to one mounted instance.

sections.title: Creating a component
sections.text: Creating a component The following example models a small status panel in an application shell. Itkeeps its own state, listens to the external window object only while it ismounted, and can be unmounted and mounted again without losing that state. The essential shape is: For one-off DOM nodes, use e() directly. When a piece of UI owns state,lifecycle, or reusable behavior, use Component or one of the componentfactories such as cbutton().

sections.title: Composition with e() and component factories
sections.text: Composition with e() and component factories e() creates native elements and accepts nested children. Component factoriessuch as cbutton() return Components, so both forms can be composed in thesame tree: The complete API is available in the Component API reference,including ComponentOptions,ComponentChild, e(),and the component factories.

sections.title: UI Styles
sections.text: UI Styles Components can use the ElgoraUI ui property to apply semantic styles andutility classes. UI Styles are documented separately, including thesemantic color system andHTML elements and utilities.

Popover Popover is a reusable floating panel. It can be positioned relative to ananchor element or at a screen point, making it useful for contextual help,menus, inspectors, and custom context-menu interactions.

sections.title: Anchored popover
sections.text: Anchored popover Pass an anchorElement and a placement to position the panel relative to anative element. The panel is a Component, so it can contain text, nativeelements, or other Components. The essential API shape is:

sections.title: Point-based popover
sections.text: Point-based popover Use setPoint(x, y) and show() when the panel should open at a pointerposition, such as after a contextmenu event. See the Popover API reference, includingPopoverOptions,PopoverPoint,PopoverPlacement, andPopoverCloseMode.
PopupMenu PopupMenu renders action menus on demand. Items can contain icons, actions,links, dividers, checked state, and asynchronously loaded nested submenus.

sections.title: Dynamic nested menu
sections.text: Dynamic nested menu Create a menu once and provide its items when the trigger is activated. Thiskeeps menu content close to the action that opens it and allows submenus to beloaded only when needed.

sections.title: Context menu
sections.text: Context menu The same menu can be opened at the pointer by passing a point to show(). See the PopupMenu API reference,PopupMenuOptions,PopupMenuShowOptions,MenuItem, andRemixIcon.
Resizable elements — ResizeHandle ResizeHandle adds resizing to a positioned element without owning its content. Try dragging the corner of the Popover demo.

sections.title: Configure a resize handle
sections.text: Configure a resize handle The demo also uses ResizeHandle to resize the panelfrom its bottom-right corner. It captures the pointer, constrains dimensions tothe viewport and retains inline dimensions when the panel is reopened. The helper changes border-box dimensions, not panel positioning. Use a positionedtarget with flexible content; dispose the helper with its owner.

sections.title: Ownership
sections.text: Ownership Register the helper with its owner through addCleanup. Dispose it before removing an independently managed target. Resizing changes inline dimensions, not application data or the target’s placement policy. API: ResizeHandle, ResizeHandleOptions.

Scroll Engine ScrollEngine enhances an existing viewport with virtual dimensions andcustom scrolling. It keeps the physical viewport small even when the logicalcontent is very large, and exposes coordinates and scroll events to the hostapplication. For ordinary HTML overflow containers, use Scrollbarsto keep native browser scrolling while applying the same scrollbar appearance.

sections.title: Programmatic scrolling
sections.text: Programmatic scrolling Create the viewport first, then pass it to ScrollEngine. CallupdateDimensions() with the logical content size and use scrollTo() whenapplication code needs to change the position. The same engine also handles wheel, keyboard, pointer, and touch input. UseonScroll() to update dependent UI and onResize() to recalculate layout. Wheel gestures are consumed only when the viewport can move in the requesteddirection. At a scroll boundary, or when that axis has no overflow, the eventremains uncancelled so a surrounding scroll container can handle it. Shift +wheel scrolls horizontally. A gesture that reaches a boundary is clamped there;the next gesture in the same direction is passed through. This also applies toDataGrid, which uses ScrollEngine internally. See the ScrollEngine API reference.

sections.title: Scrollbar appearance
sections.text: Scrollbar appearance scrollbarMode controls the presentation of overflowing axes: "thin" (default): a 3px thumb remains visible, including during scrolling.Moving near its edge or dragging expands it to 12px. "auto": hidden at rest, full-width near its edge or during scrolling and dragging. "always": full-width whenever the axis has overflow. The pointer hit area stays 12px wide in all modes. Only the painted thumb becomesthinner, so dragging and track clicks keep the same geometry. An axis withoutoverflow stays hidden regardless of the selected mode. In auto mode, thescrollbar hides 600ms after scrolling ends, unless the pointer is nearby or dragging. scrollbarHoverDistance defaults to 50 CSS pixels. Inside the viewport, thevertical scrollbar expands near the right edge and the horizontal scrollbar nearthe bottom edge, independently. Both expand near the bottom-right corner. Set 0to expand only when directly hovering a scrollbar. Non-negative finite values areaccepted; changing the setting rechecks the current pointer position. DataGrid exposes the same option, including runtime updates: See ScrollEngineOptions andScrollbarMode.

sections.title: Fixed header space
sections.text: Fixed header space Use verticalScrollbarTop to place the vertical track below a fixed header. Thevalue is a non-negative finite number in CSS pixels, defaulting to 0: The inset shortens the track and adjusts the thumb to represent the remainingbody area. It does not change virtual scroll coordinates, the maximum scrollposition, or fire onScroll. Track clicks and dragging still reach both ends.An inset covering the whole viewport hides the vertical track; reducing it makesthe track available again when content overflows. DataGrid manages this automatically from its complete table-header height:column headers, the filter row and all rendered sticky group/tree rows. Thegroup panel is already outside the scroll viewport. The scrollbar’s pointerarea therefore never covers those header controls, including the last column’sresize handle. No grid-specific configuration is required. API: ScrollEngine.verticalScrollbarTop.

ScrollSpy ScrollSpy connects navigation links to headings in an existing content element.The “On this page” navigation in these documentation topics uses it. Scroll thispage or click a section link to see the active section change.

sections.title: Basic usage
sections.text: Basic usage Use unique IDs on the headings and matching anchor links in the navigation.The component adds no wrapper elements and does not render the navigation.

sections.title: Scroll containers
sections.text: Scroll containers By default the scroll viewport is the window. Set scrollContainer when thecontent is inside a separately scrolling panel. Both the content and itsnavigation may be placed inside that panel; sticky positioning is configuredthrough CSS, independently of ScrollSpy. The last heading above the activation line is active. Before the first heading,the first section is active. At the bottom of a scrollable viewport, the lastsection becomes active even when it is too short to reach the activation line.Hidden targets, missing targets and links to other documents are ignored.

sections.title: Active appearance
sections.text: Active appearance The current link receives aria-current="location" and the classelg-scroll-spy-active. Supply activeClass to use a different class.Styling remains under the application’s control, for example: When the navigation itself scrolls, ScrollSpy keeps the newly active linkvisible without scrolling the surrounding page. It does not intercept anchorclicks, move keyboard focus, or change the URL during scrolling.

sections.title: Refresh and disposal
sections.text: Refresh and disposal Scroll and resize updates are batched through the ElgoraUI scheduler. Contentsize changes are observed automatically. After adding, removing or renamingheadings or links, call refresh() to rescan their associations. Disposal removes listeners and observers and restores the navigation’s originalactive classes and aria-current attributes.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See ScrollSpy andScrollSpyOptions.

Native scrollbars Scrollbars gives native scroll containers the same scrollbar appearance asScrollEngine. The browser still scrolls the content:wheel, touch gestures, keyboard navigation, text selection and scrollIntoView()continue to work normally. No wrapper is inserted around the content.

sections.title: Automatic installation
sections.text: Automatic installation The example installs scrollbars for its sandbox window. Try the native panel,the textarea and the page scrollbar. Add a panel to see automatic discovery.Enable Local to keep panels in always-visible mode while the global controlscontinue to affect the page and textarea. Disable Local to resume the globalsettings. Turning Global off disposes only the global installation; an enabledlocal installation continues to work. Scroll positions are preserved. Installation discovers containers with overflow: auto or overflow: scroll,including containers that gain overflow later. A Window installation also handlesthe document’s scrolling element. New elements and layout changes are reconciled through theElgoraUI frame scheduler. ScrollEngine viewports and their descendants are skipped.Call installation.refresh() after application-specific changes that do not emitDOM or resize notifications.

sections.title: Container scopes and ownership
sections.text: Container scopes and ownership install(container) enhances the container itself and its descendants. It leavesthe rest of the document alone, making it suitable for dialogs or embedded views: Ownership follows these priorities, regardless of creation order: An explicit Scrollbars.attach(element) owns that element’s scrollbar. The closest container installation owns the other native scroll viewports in its scope. A Window installation is the fallback for the remaining document. Nested installations do not duplicate controls. Ownership transfers reuse theexisting overlay and preserve scroll position. Disposing an outer installationdoes not dispose a deeper installation or an explicit attachment. New descendantsand moved containers are reconciled automatically.

sections.title: Attach to one container
sections.text: Attach to one container Set up native overflow and a bounded size, then attach: Scrollbars.attach(window) enhances only the page scrollbar. attach(textarea)also works; user input and resizing refresh its scroll geometry. A programmatictextarea.value change can be followed by handle.refresh(). Repeated calls to attach() for an element return the same handle. Repeatedinstall() calls for the same Window or container return the same installation.If options are provided again, they update its presentation. Dispose when the owner is released;these calls do not create independent ownership counts. An automatic installation leaves explicit attachments alone, includingtheir mode and disposal. Calling attach() on an automatically managed elementreturns its current handle and promotes it to explicit ownership. Further changesor disposal of installations do not affect that handle. If the explicit handle isdisposed while an installation still covers the element, automatic discovery canenhance it again on the next scheduled reconciliation. The helper preserves the target’s inline styles and DOMchildren. An axis without overflow has no scrollbar.

sections.title: Appearance and scope
sections.text: Appearance and scope scrollbarMode supports "thin" (default), "auto" and "always", with the same3px idle thumb and 12px pointer hit area as ScrollEngine. Pointer proximity anddragging expand the thumb in thin mode; scrolling alone leaves it thin. In automode, scrolling also reveals the otherwise hidden scrollbar. Both adapters share the painting andpointer interaction implementation. scrollbarHoverDistance defaults to 50 CSS pixels from the viewport’s right orbottom edge. Each axis expands independently; the middle of the content staysvisually quiet. 0 means direct scrollbar hover only. The option is available onattach(), install() and their returned handles, and accepts non-negative finitenumbers. Moving the pointer away restores the idle appearance unless draggingis still active (or scrolling in auto mode). Proximity changes width only;direct hover and dragging make the thumb more opaque. Each installation handles its scope in one document’s ordinary HTML tree. It does not traverseiframe documents or shadow roots. Call Scrollbars.install(iframe.contentWindow)from code with access to that document to enhance it separately. Native controlswhose internal scroll areas are not exposed as DOM elements are browser-managed.Scroll containers with rotations or scaled transforms are not supported.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference Scrollbars,ScrollbarsOptions,ScrollbarsHandle,ScrollbarsInstallation,ScrollbarMode.

Time and DateTime editors TimeEditor and DateTimeEditor use the same value, validation and asynchronousconfirmation lifecycle as the other Value editors.They do not convert values to a timezone or create a JavaScript Date object. Both editors include a button for mouse and touch input. The picker uses onevertical list of time slots, every 15 minutes by default. Set minuteStep to5, 10, 30 or another divisor of 60 when a different precision is needed.When the value is empty, defaultTime controls the initially focused slot anddefaults to 10:00.

sections.title: TimeEditor
sections.text: TimeEditor TimeEditor stores a 24-hour value as HH:mm by default. Use HH:mm:ss whenseconds are significant. Empty input resolves to null. The parser rejects invalid clock values such as 24:00 or 12:60. timeFormatcontrols the accepted layout and is limited to HH:mm and HH:mm:ss.

sections.title: DateTimeEditor
sections.text: DateTimeEditor DateTimeEditor stores a local date-time without timezone information. Itscanonical value is YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm or YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss; the input uses aspace between the date and time for readability. Its picker displays the calendar and time slots side by side. Keyboard focusstarts in the calendar and continues to the time list with Tab; ArrowUpand ArrowDown move between time slots. If the date-time has no time yet,defaultTime supplies the time used after selecting a date. The date part follows DateFormatter; the time part follows TimeFormatter.Invalid dates, invalid clock values and ambiguous input are rejected beforevalidation or onCommit runs.

sections.title: Confirmation and validation
sections.text: Confirmation and validation Both editors accept the common validate, onCommit, commit() and cancel()options. A failed validation or save leaves the typed value available forcorrection and retry. DateEditor, TimeEditor, DateTimeEditor and LookupEditor share thePopoverEditor base class. open() and close() control picker visibility;closing neither accepts nor discards the draft. A picker choice closes the panelimmediately and starts confirmation independently. Errors appear on the editorwithout reopening the panel. Escape cancels the draft and returns to the input. Use resolveText() for conversion only. It does not change the editor value,invoke business validation or call the save callback.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference See the API references for TimeEditor,DateTimeEditor andTimeFormatter.
Tooltip Tooltip.attach() adds a small description to an anchor. It supports pointerhover and keyboard focus, accepts plain text or rich content, and returns acleanup function for temporary UI.

sections.title: Attach a tooltip
sections.text: Attach a tooltip Attach a tooltip to any suitable native element or Component DOM root. Theplacement and delay are optional.

sections.title: Rich content
sections.text: Rich content Tooltip content can be a string, an HTMLElement, a Component, or anothersupported typed content value. Call the returned cleanup function when the anchor is removed or the tooltipis no longer needed. See the Tooltip API reference,TooltipContent, andTooltipShowOptions.

TreeView Use TreeView<T> for navigation, document outlines and hierarchical pickers.It is a standalone component built on VirtualList, not a one-column DataGrid.Only visible rows are rendered; expanded items and loaded children remain in memory.

sections.title: Lazy asynchronous branches
sections.text: Lazy asynchronous branches Expand Pages and Media to load their children. Retry example deliberatelyfails once: its inline Retry button reloads only that branch. The request counteralso demonstrates that collapsing and reopening a successful branch uses its cache.Use Show nested example to open Pages → Guides → Getting started → Tutorials.Mixed folders and leaves across five levels demonstrate indentation and reserveddisclosure space; a long title also exercises single-line truncation.The custom renderer adds open/closed folder icons and page/image icons withoutchanging the accessible labels or TreeView’s disclosure controls.

sections.title: Data adapter
sections.text: Data adapter getChildren(undefined, signal) requests roots. Every call returns all immediatechildren, either as an array or a Promise. Pagination is not part of this contract.Keys must be globally unique, stable strings, including across different parents.hasChildren must be available before loading a branch; a successfully loaded emptybranch loses its disclosure arrow. Loading and error rows belong to their branch and do not replace the rest of thetree. Concurrent requests for the same branch are shared. Collapsing retains bothcached children and in-flight work; reopening does not start a duplicate request.

sections.title: Cache and lifetime
sections.text: Cache and lifetime Mounting starts root loading. load() can also start it explicitly and shares theexisting request. expand(item) loads a known item’s children when needed;collapse(item) hides descendants without discarding them. await tree.refresh(item) invalidates and reloads a branch’s descendants;await tree.refresh() reloads the whole tree. Stable keys retain expansion andselection when their items are loaded again. A missing selected item clears theselection after loading finishes. Refresh aborts invalidated requests. Disposeaborts all requests, and late responses are ignored even if a loader ignores its signal. Loader failures are shown locally rather than rejected from load, expand orrefresh. Do not use their Promise fulfillment as proof that a remote request succeeded.TreeView does not infer external data changes: call refresh when the adapter changes.

sections.title: Focus, selection and activation
sections.text: Focus, selection and activation Focus and selection are independent. Arrow Up/Down and Home/End move focus;Right opens a branch or enters its first child, and Left collapses it or movesto its parent. Typing a label prefix finds a visible item. Space selects;Enter selects and activates. Clicking selects; double-clicking activates. Subscribe to selectionChanged, focusedItemChanged and itemActivated forthese separate actions. itemContextMenu lets the host provide its own menu.The tree exposes ARIA levels, sibling positions, expansion and selection state. select(item) selects a loaded item without moving browser focus.await reveal(item) opens its known ancestors and scrolls to it, also withoutstealing browser focus. It returns false for an unknown item: a remote adapter mustload its ancestor path first. There is no automatic remote path search.

sections.title: Custom rows
sections.text: Custom rows renderItem can populate the row’s content host with an icon, tag and secondarytext. Keep content non-interactive: TreeView owns disclosure, keyboard focus andselection. Always provide getText for the accessible label and type-ahead.This version uses fixed 30px, single-line rows; custom content must fit that height. The HtmlEditor demo also uses TreeView to navigatethe editor’s model elements. Structural element selection and the full propertyinspector are separate, later stages.
Checkbox editor CheckboxEditor produces boolean values usinga native checkbox. It uses the same validation and acceptance contractas text-based editors.

sections.title: Shipping confirmation
sections.text: Shipping confirmation Click the checkbox or focus it and press Space. Each change is acceptedasynchronously; the control is unavailable until the callback completes.

sections.title: Boolean values and external text
sections.text: Boolean values and external text The label option gives the control an accessible name; add a visible label inthe surrounding form. User changes confirm immediately rather than waiting forEnter or blur. Failed validation or acceptance retains an unaccepted draft. resolveText() accepts true/false, yes/no, and 1/0, ignoring case andsurrounding whitespace. Empty or unsupported text throws. For localized text,provide your own converter:

sections.text: API reference CheckboxEditor,ValueEditorOptions,ValueEditor.
Values, confirmation and callbacks

sections.title: Shared contract
sections.text: Shared contract Typing changes a draft; confirmedValue changes only after parsing, validationand onCommit succeed. modified includes unparsed text changes.commit() returns Promise<boolean>; a failure retains the draft and exposeserror. Correct it or retry. cancel() restores the last accepted value.setValue() silently loads an external value as a new baseline. validate and onCommit can be asynchronous. While either runs, busy is trueand the control is unavailable. Concurrent commits share one operation;cancel() returns false while busy, and setValue() throws. An unchanged valuedoes not call onCommit. Invalid fields have a danger-colored border. input, committed and cancelled are synchronous notification events.Use onCommit for work that must be awaited. Values are retained by reference;equality defaults to Object.is, or supply equals. Editors do not undo externalside effects: callbacks must manage their own recovery or transaction.

sections.title: Keyboard and popup behavior
sections.text: Keyboard and popup behavior Text and number editors accept Enter or leaving the field by default; usecommitOnBlur: false when the form controls confirmation. Escape cancels.IME Enter does not confirm. Native text-navigation keys remain available. Popup trigger buttons do not add a Tab stop. Alt+Down opens a picker.openOnFocus defaults to false. When enabled, DateEditor focuses DatePicker;LookupEditor retains input focus for searching. Escape returns to text editingwithout reopening DatePicker. See each editor’s topic for picker navigation.

sections.title: Resolve external text
sections.text: Resolve external text Every editor exposes resolveText(text): T | Promise<T> for clipboard/importconversion without editing, validation, saving or events. Failed conversionthrows or rejects. The host separately validates and applies the result. Text editors use resolveText, then parse, then their default conversion.Number editors support decimal dot/comma; boolean editors accept true/false,yes/no and 1/0. Lookup requires a unique match; Date uses its configured pattern.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference ValueEditor,ValueEditorOptions,TextEditorOptions,PopoverEditorOptions.
Number editor NumberEditor shares theeditor lifecycle and produces number | null.

sections.title: Order quantity
sections.text: Order quantity Try 12,5, 12.5, zero or empty text. Use ArrowUp and ArrowDown to change thedraft by one step. Positive numbers are accepted; failed validation keeps theinput available for correction.

sections.title: Conversion and validation
sections.text: Conversion and validation The default parser accepts a decimal dot or comma, resolves empty input to null,and rejects malformed/non-finite numbers. It does not interpret locale groupingseparators. Supply parse/format or resolveText for custom conversion. The input is text-based with a decimal keyboard hint, not a native number spinner.ArrowUp and ArrowDown change the draft by step and respect min/max withoutcommitting. Enter confirms, Escape cancels, and blur confirms by default. SetcommitOnBlur: false when a containing form handles confirmation.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference NumberEditor,TextEditorOptions,ValueEditor.
Text editor TextEditor edits strings or typed values throughtext. See the overview for the shared lifecycle.

sections.title: Order reference
sections.text: Order reference Enter a reference, press Enter or leave the field to accept it. Empty text failsvalidation; Escape restores the last accepted reference.

sections.title: Text and typed values
sections.text: Text and typed values text is raw input; value is parsed during confirmation. For non-string initialvalues, provide parse or resolveText, and normally a matching format: Enter confirms; Escape cancels. Arrow keys remain native caret operations.IME Enter does not confirm. Blur confirms unless commitOnBlur is false.resolveText takes precedence over parse; both may be asynchronous.External resolveText() only converts text and does not save or validate.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference TextEditor,TextEditorOptions,ValueEditor.
Toggle editor ToggleEditor is a compact switch with a slidingthumb and theme colors. It shares the editor lifecycleand boolean conversion of CheckboxEditor.

sections.title: Priority order
sections.text: Priority order Click the switch or use Space/Enter. Its state is accepted asynchronously.

sections.title: Configure a switch
sections.text: Configure a switch The track uses role="switch" and aria-checked. Place a visible label besideit; label supplies the accessible name. Native Space/Enter activation togglesand confirms the value. Animation respects reduced-motion preferences. Validation, busy state, errors, cancel() and setValue() work as for othereditors. resolveText() accepts true/false, yes/no and 1/0, or a custom converter,without changing the switch or calling the external callback.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference ToggleEditor,ValueEditorOptions,ValueEditor.

Editor validation Every value editor accepts a validate callback. It may return an error messageor a promise that resolves to one. A failed validation keeps the draft value andmarks the editor as invalid. The compact error icon at the start of an inputshows the message in a tooltip without changing the form layout.

sections.title: Try invalid values
sections.text: Try invalid values Each editor starts with an invalid draft so the validation UI is visibleimmediately. Correct a value and press Enter, or toggle a boolean back on, toclear its error. The lookup demonstrates a failed text resolution, while thedate editor demonstrates a syntactically invalid calendar date. The validate option is configured per editor. It may be synchronous orasynchronous and returns an error message when the current value is notaccepted. Text and number editors validate typed values, checkbox and toggleeditors validate boolean values, and lookup/date editors can report errorsfrom text resolution before the value is accepted.

sections.title: Shared contract
sections.text: Shared contract Validation runs after text conversion and before onCommit. It can besynchronous or asynchronous. While it runs, the editor is busy and unavailable.The error is exposed through editor.error, the control receivesaria-invalid="true", and the validation icon exposes the same message throughits tooltip and accessible description. Use editor.cancel() to restore the last accepted value, or correct the draftand call editor.commit() again. Validation does not write to a data source.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference ValueEditor,ValueEditorOptions,TextEditor,NumberEditor,CheckboxEditor,ToggleEditor,LookupEditor,DateEditor.

Value editors Editors work with values, not rows or data sources. Use them in forms, dialogsor grids. The external onCommit callback decides whether acceptance updatesa local model, applies a business operation or saves remotely.

sections.title: Try the editors
sections.text: Try the editors This small order form demonstrates all eight editor types without a code editor.Change a field to see its accepted value below. Quantity must be positive;callbacks simulate asynchronous acceptance. Enter confirms text, Escape restoresthe accepted value, and checkbox/toggle changes confirm immediately.

sections.title: Choose an editor
sections.text: Choose an editor Text: strings and custom text conversion. Number: nullable numeric input and validation. Checkbox: native boolean control. Toggle: compact switch control. Lookup: search and select an item from a virtualized list. Date: formatted date-only input and DatePicker picker. Time and DateTime: time slots and a combined calendar/time picker. HTML editor: edit rich-text HTML and accept or discard the draft. Each sub-topic contains an editable demo, configuration examples, keyboardbehavior and links to its API reference. DatePickerremains a standalone component and can be used without DateEditor.

sections.title: Related topics
sections.text: Related topics Values, confirmation and callbacks Validation and errors Time and DateTime demos
Virtual List VirtualList renders only the rows that are visible in the viewport. This keepsthe DOM small even when the underlying collection contains hundreds ofthousands of items.

sections.title: Variable-height rows
sections.text: Variable-height rows The demo below renders 100,000 generated rows. Each row has a different height,while VirtualList measures and positions only the visible portion of thecollection. The data source provides random access through getAt() and the total numberof rows through count(). renderRow() receives the row element, data, andvisible index so the application can render the row content. See the VirtualList API reference, includingVirtualListOptions,DataList, and RenderRowArgs.

Localization Use locale to control regional presentation and to supply a consistent contextto editors and their pickers. Use an application-local Localization instance,or the optional Localization.default singleton for convenient global settings. This first step provides locale inheritance, not a translation system. Built-incommands, validation messages and labels such as Today remain unchanged. Currency,timezones, the calendar’s first weekday and input-acceptance rules are not inferredfrom the locale. Tolerant, locale-aware parsing will be a separate step.

sections.title: Priority and inheritance
sections.text: Priority and inheritance Consumer Resolution order Grid cell and its editor Column locale → grid locale → grid localization or Localization.default → runtime locale Standalone editor Editor locale → editor localization or Localization.default → runtime locale Standalone DatePicker DatePicker locale → calendar localization or Localization.default → runtime locale Editor’s DatePicker, TimePicker or lookup grid Resolved editor locale; lookup result columns may override their own locale Unset options stay unset. The grid does not write its inherited locale intocolumn definitions or its options. undefined restores inheritance; an emptystring is not an inheritance marker. Locales use BCP 47 identifiers such asbg-BG, en-US and de-DE. A context canonicalizes identifiers and rejectsmalformed identifiers without changing its previous value.

sections.title: Global or application-local settings
sections.text: Global or application-local settings Independent applications or sections can share a context without changing thesingleton or affecting one another: Contexts emit their new locale through changed. Subscribers receive changes,not an initial notification. Read .locale for the current setting. The gridand DatePicker own their subscriptions and unsubscribe on disposal. Replacing agrid’s context via setOptions({ localization: anotherContext }) detaches the oldsubscription. Callers own contexts and should not dispose a context’s sharedchanged event while other components use it.

sections.title: Try regional presentation
sections.text: Try regional presentation Change the application locale below. Amount, Date and the standalone calendarinherit it; USD stays en-US. Double-click a grid cell to edit it. No translationor new text-parsing behavior is enabled by this demo.

sections.title: Grid editor context
sections.text: Grid editor context The grid passes the resolved locale to createFieldEditor for both normalediting and clipboard paste. The adapter resolves the column override once,then passes the same string to built-in editors and to the custom factory’sFieldEditorContext.locale. Row-bound resolveText, validate, lookup andeditable formatValue callbacks receive that snapshot too. Custom factories must forward it to their editor: An editor captures its locale at creation and retains it for its lifetime.For grid editors this is one editing session: changing global, application orgrid locale does not replace the active editor, rewrite its input or change itsinterpretation halfway through editing. The next editor receives the new locale.Standalone editors follow the same lifetime rule; recreate one to adopt a newlocale. Their nested pickers use the captured locale, including popovers firstopened after a context change.

sections.title: Display, data and input stay separate
sections.text: Display, data and input stay separate Inherited locale controls built-in displayFormat presentation for grid data,group summaries and totals. Changes do not reload the source, alter group keys,discard selection/expansion, cancel pending rows or replace invalid cell inputs.Auto columns are remeasured for the new labels. Custom getText/lookup labelsremain application-owned and are not automatically reloaded; refresh their datawhen their language-dependent labels change. locale replaces the earlier field property displayLocale; no compatibilityalias is retained. The grid overview now sets its locale once, at grid level. Stored values and existing parsers remain unchanged. NumberEditor still acceptsits existing decimal-dot/comma input, DateEditor keeps its configured dateFormat(including locale-dependent d), and TimeEditor retains HH:mm[:ss]. Locale doesnot automatically enable grouped/currency input or localized checkbox words.Explicit resolveText, parse, format and formatValue callbacks retain theirexisting precedence. A currency suffix such as C2€ remains literal, regardlessof the locale. Standalone NumberFormatter/DateFormatter continue accepting theirown explicit locale arguments; pass localization.locale when needed. See Numbers, dates and formatting for display patterns andexplicit converters.

Undo and redo UndoCoordinator is the single owner of undo/redo execution. Individual history scopesrecord already-applied operations, but cannot independently undo or clear them.One chronological journal can combine DataSet edits with view and application actions.

sections.title: Try shared data and view histories
sections.text: Try shared data and view histories Edit the amount and leave the field or click Apply amount, then toggle the view. Undo reverses whichever action happened last.Save data clears only the dataset scope; view operations remain undoable. Watch thescope flags and the per-scope baseline log.

sections.title: Create a coordinator and a history scope
sections.text: Create a coordinator and a history scope record() does not execute the action: it records an action that has already succeeded.Capture before/after values rather than reading mutable state inside a later redo.Operations may return void or Promise. A failed replay must leave applicationstate unchanged so it can safely be retried.

sections.title: One chronological journal, multiple scopes
sections.text: One chronological journal, multiple scopes Use only coordinator.undo(), coordinator.redo() and coordinator.clear(history).Scopes expose canUndo and canRedo, but neither selects which global action is next.Duplicate scope names do not imply shared state. A new record after undo removes the complete global redo branch, including entriesfrom other scopes. This keeps chronology consistent.

sections.title: Saving establishes a new baseline
sections.text: Saving establishes a new baseline clear(history) removes both applied and redo entries belonging to that scope.It does not undo data and does not signal returnedToBaseline. Do not clear beforepersistence succeeds: failed saves must retain the user’s ability to undo.

sections.title: Returning to a scope’s baseline
sections.text: Returning to a scope’s baseline returnedToBaseline fires after undo removes the last applied operation in a scope.Other scopes may still have applied operations. Redo followed by undo can reachthe same scope baseline again. The coordinator waits for registered baseline work before accepting another action.Do not edit the dataset, record, clear or replay history in a baseline handler:the coordinator is busy. DataSet already restores its recorded data; it does notneed rejectChanges() when its history reaches the baseline. The waitUntil API here belongs to UndoBaselineEvent. It is separate from DataSetbusiness events, whose async subscribers are awaited directly through invokeAsync().

sections.title: Async operations and failure handling
sections.text: Async operations and failure handling During replay busy is true. Concurrent undo/redo, record and clear are rejected.DataSet also guards its edits against coordinator replay, saving and active transactions.Use ensureIdle() before changing application state, not only before recording it. If undo or redo fails, the journal position remains unchanged. The operation mustitself preserve or restore its previous state. In contrast, afterReplay and baselineobservers run after the replay position is committed: an observer error rejects thecall but does not reverse the completed action or move the cursor back. For remote persistence, an undo callback cannot erase a server request that alreadycommitted. Decide separately whether your application supports compensating serveroperations. DataSet’s standard history is for local edits before save.

sections.title: Update toolbar state
sections.text: Update toolbar state Each scope also exposes changed with record, undo, redo and clear notifications.Unlike DataSet events, UndoHistory.changed passesthe notification name directly to its subscriber, not an object with a kind property: Value Meaning record An already-applied operation was added; the global redo branch is discarded undo One operation belonging to this scope was undone redo One operation belonging to this scope was redone clear Applied and redo entries for this scope were removed without replay UndoCoordinator.changed has no payload:read busy, canUndo and canRedo from the coordinator.The demo log shows these scope values and separate baseline notifications. Observers must not synchronously mutate the journal. Dispose subscriptions whentheir UI consumer is destroyed.

sections.title: DataSet integration
sections.text: DataSet integration DataTable exposes its dataset’s coordinator through the DataSource contract, sodifferent components can use the same journal. A successful DataSet transactionrecords one operation, even if business rules changed several rows and tables.Replay restores stored row versions and emits reset notifications, withoutrerunning business rules. Read DataSet for pending new rows, validation, transactions and save.

sections.title: API reference
sections.text: API reference UndoCoordinator — shared journal and replay commands UndoHistory — scope state and notifications UndoOperation — undo, redo and post-replay callbacks UndoBaselineEvent — asynchronous baseline cleanup DataSet — automatic data history integration UndoCoordinator API

ArrayDataSource ArrayDataSource reads and edits the supplied array directly. Existing objectsretain their references; new rows are plain objects. There is no server request,batch save or undo history.

sections.title: Product list
sections.text: Product list Use Add product, Edit and Delete. The form collects input until OK.A new product stays outside the list until its session is inserted; Canceldiscards the draft. Expand Change notifications to see the event kind, rowand current values. The demo’s form validation belongs to the UI; it is not an ArrayDataSource businessrule. Direct changes to the public array or its objects do not emit changed.Use the mutation methods when consumers need notifications.

sections.title: Configure defaults and identities
sections.text: Configure defaults and identities idField defaults to id. The generated identity overrides the same member indefaults and cannot be changed through update(). Factories may be asynchronous;multiple drafts can coexist. Duplicate identities are rejected, including identitiesreserved by another pending session. API: ArrayDataSource,ArrayDataSourceOptions.

sections.title: Read and edit
sections.text: Read and edit API: loadData,update,delete,createNewRow,NewRowSession. Update/delete operate on the source’s actual row reference, not a newly constructedobject with the same ID. Pending rows can be updated but must be cancelled ratherthan deleted. Repeated successful insert/cancel calls are harmless; switching froman inserted session to cancel, or from a cancelled session to insert, rejects.

sections.title: Local query processing
sections.text: Local query processing loadData() filters and sorts before paging; total summaries use the completefiltered result, not just the returned page. Sorting never reorders the suppliedarray, and returned pages have their own array container while retaining row references.The grid provides local grouping throughLocalGroupingDataSource. For calculated fields, prefer a synchronous accessor when the value is alreadyavailable locally: Async accessors and custom summary callbacks are also supported and awaited inorder. Accessors and summary callbacks must not change source data. A local querymay read a field once per row and reuse that value for several summaries,including group and total summaries. Completed query results can be reused untilthe source is invalidated; see cache invalidation. See DataField andSummaryDefinition.

sections.title: Related topics
sections.text: Related topics Local processing and cache invalidation Queries, grouping and summaries

Local processing and cache invalidation ArrayDataSource and DataTable keep bounded query caches; LocalGroupingDataSource reuses grouped results against the source revision. Keep accessors and summaries pure. Returned page arrays are independent containers, but row objects and field values are not cloned.

sections.title: ArrayDataSource cache
sections.text: ArrayDataSource cache ArrayDataSource caches complete filtered/sorted row lists and total summaries.Changing skip, top or requireTotalCount reuses the complete result insteadof processing the array again. Each local cache retains at most eight queries,evicting the least recently used entry. Returned page arrays and summary recordsare separate containers; row objects and object-valued results retain their references. Successful updates to confirmed rows, newRowSession.insert() and delete()increment revision and invalidate thecaches before emitting changed. Failed operations and equal-value updates donot invalidate. Pending-row creation, edits and cancellation do not invalidatenormal queries because pending rows are excluded from them. Direct changes to the public array or its objects are not tracked. Explicitlyinvalidate after those changes: invalidateCache() incrementsthe revision, clears local query results and emits { kind: "reset" }. Connectedgrids can then reload. Refreshing a grid alone does not invalidate the source.Also call this method when changing external data captured by an accessor,filter function or custom summary, or replacing a configured filter function. LocalGroupingDataSource uses the ArrayDataSource revision to cache complete groupresults, counts and summaries independently for each adapter. It detects changesto relevant field metadata and callback identities; captured external values stillrequire source invalidation. Paging through groups does not regroup the rows.The adapter also supports DataTable’s local revision and caches,but does not cache remote sources.Failed/cancelled calculations and calculations completed after a revision changeare not stored in the query-result cache.

sections.title: Observe changes
sections.text: Observe changes The event kinds are create, update, insert, delete, cancel and reset.Only update supplies changed field names. Equal-value updates emit no event.create means a draft was initialized; insert means it joined the array. API: changed,DataSourceChanged. For related tables, reversible business rules or a batch to send to a server, useDataSet instead.

sections.title: DataTable cache
sections.text: DataTable cache DataTable queries read DataRow values directly. Filtering, sorting and summariesdo not convert rows into plain objects or replace their references. Pending anddeleted rows are excluded from pages, counts and summaries. API: DataTable.loadData(),QueryArgs,DataRow.getValue(). Complete filtered/sorted row lists and totals are cached in bounded local caches(up to eight entries each). The grid’s LocalGroupingDataSource also caches completegroup results against the table’srevision, so paging does not regroup the table.Sorting reads each sort field once per row before comparing keys. Row objects andfield values are not cloned; returned pages have independent array containers. Confirmed-row updates, insertion and deletion invalidate queries at the pointthe working data changes, before rowChanged business handlers run. A query insidea transaction therefore sees the current working values, including derived editsalready applied. Queries do not provide an isolated snapshot across asynchronousmutations. UI changed notifications remain deferred until successful commit. Rollback, undo/redo, import, acceptance/rejection and server ID mapping alsoinvalidate automatically. Revision numbers advance on invalidation; undo does notrestore an earlier revision number. Pending-only edits and equal-value updates donot invalidate confirmed-row queries. Failed/cancelled async calculations, orcalculations completed after the revision changed, are not cached. Use DataTable.invalidateCache()while the dataset is idle after changing external dependencies captured by customaccessors/summaries, or after an in-place object modification. It increments therevision and emits { kind: "reset" }, but does not record an edit or undo operation.In-place object changes are still not tracked for persistence or rollback; normallyreplace a field through setValue() instead. Refreshing a grid alone does notinvalidate table caches. Dependencies captured from another table are not detectedautomatically; stored calculated fields should be updated through business rules.

DataSource A DataSource connects a view to its working data. It can read an array, call anHTTP API or expose a DataTable. Consumers work with the same query contractwithout depending on the storage implementation. Start with ArrayDataSource for local records, orCustom remote source for a paged catalog.Both examples use a simple table so the data-source behavior is visible withoutrequiring a DataGrid.

sections.title: Reading data
sections.text: Reading data Only loadData(args) is required: The api in this snippet is an application-owned client. See the remote examplefor a complete implementation with a simulated endpoint. API: DataSource.loadData,QueryArgs, DataResult. The query may contain filtering, sorting, paging, grouping and summary requests.Return the original args with the result. When requested, totalCount describesall matching rows or groups before paging, not the size of the returned page.Total summaries similarly cover the complete filtered set. A remote source canomit count/summary computation when those values are not requested. See DataFilter for filter structures and local evaluation,FilterEditor for the visual playground, andQueries, grouping and summaries for the complete grouped protocol. For grouping, a supported query returns groups (including an empty array forno matches). If grouping is unsupported, return neither groups nor dataItemsfor that request. LocalGroupingDataSourcecan then request flat data and provide local grouping. A remote fallback mustmake the complete matching data available; a single server page cannot producecomplete groups or totals.

sections.title: Optional capabilities
sections.text: Optional capabilities Capability Purpose update(row, values) Apply a field patch to an existing or pending row delete(row) Delete a confirmed row createNewRow() Initialize a pending editing session changed Notify consumers when working data changes undoCoordinator Expose history owned by the source/application getRowId(row) Provide a stable row identity hasChildren(row) Declare hierarchical data and per-row expandability Missing mutation methods mean the corresponding operation is unavailable.An adapter must preserve that distinction rather than advertise methods thatits underlying source cannot execute. API: DataSource,MutationResult,DataSourceChanged.

sections.title: New rows
sections.text: New rows A new-row session owns the actual draft row. Initialize it, edit it throughthe source, and explicitly insert or cancel: Drafts are excluded from ordinary queries until insertion. Session state ispending, inserted or cancelled. Expected update/delete/insert validationfailures resolve with success: false; initialization, cancellation and unexpectedfailures reject their Promises. Await commands and check their results beforeclosing an editor or starting a dependent operation. API: NewRowSession,insert,cancel.

sections.title: Notifications and persistence
sections.text: Notifications and persistence changed describes working-data changes, not necessarily server persistence.Consumers subscribe and dispose their subscription when destroyed. ArrayDataSourcenotifies for edits to pending rows too; a consumer can update an open form withoutadding the draft to its table. DataSource does not prescribe a batch-save API. A remote implementation can persistfrom its mutation methods; ArrayDataSource changes memory immediately. UseDataSet for local batch edits, business rules, transactions andundo/redo, then save the accumulated dataset changes explicitly.

Queries, grouping and summaries A source receives QueryArgs and returns a DataResult. Flat queries apply filtering and sorting before skip/top. requireTotalCount requests the filtered count before paging. Projection limits returned fields, not the data used to filter or aggregate. Pass abortSignal to remote transport and check it before publishing results.

sections.title: Grouped loadData queries
sections.text: Grouped loadData queries QueryArgs.groupBy describes one or more levels, outermost first. A normalsingle-level request and an expand-all request use the same contract: count always counts data records in a bucket, not child groups. Every non-leafbucket contains the complete next-level groups array; leaf buckets omit it.The response contains no dataItems. skip/top page only the outer groups;without top, return every outer group. Return an accurate totalCount whenrequested; expand-all checks it against the complete outer group array.Total summaries cover all matching data,not just the returned groups. An interval is explicit in its descriptor:{ field: "createdAt", interval: "month" }; omitting it applies no interval.For custom buckets, register a named interval in groupIntervals. Remote sourcesimplement the same interval name on the server. LocalGroupingDataSource constructs all requested levels in one pass over thefiltered rows. Remote sources can use server-side grouping and return the sametree; the grid has no source-specific expansion path or local-index access.Sources without grouped-query support return { args }, allowing the localadapter to request flat data once and group it. For large remote datasets,implement grouped queries to avoid transferring the complete flat result. API: QueryArgs,GroupByField,GroupItem.

sections.title: Group values and null semantics
sections.text: Group values and null semantics Grouping uses the field’s actual values without converting them according todataType. The source should provide a consistent value type per grouped field.If a source mixes numbers and numeric text and considers them equivalent, normalizethem in the source before grouping. The grid does not convert "01" into 1. null and undefined form one missing-value group, represented by null.Empty text ("") forms a separate group, as it does in databases that distinguishNULL from empty strings. 0 and false are neither missing nor empty text.Group labels show (No value) and (Empty text) respectively.Dates are not automatically converted to ISO strings. Use date intervals fordate buckets (for example, numeric month 2), or a custom interval for an explicitapplication-specific grouping value. Nonempty values, including interval results,retain their types and identity; return stable scalar buckets for complex values. Remote grouped sources return groupValue: null for missing values andgroupValue: "" for empty text. Compute counts and summaries per group beforepaging. Sources whose storage does not distinguish these values cannot recoverthat distinction; the grid preserves the values the source returns. Child queries use ordinary equality or the named interval selector, such as{ function: "year", field: "date" }. No internal key decoding is needed: Both filters round-trip through JSON unchanged. Local equality with null alsomatches missing (undefined) fields; inequality with null is its inverse(IS NOT NULL in SQL). Other equality comparisons remain type-strict.These filter rules are not a general implementation of SQL’s three-valued logic.

sections.title: Demand-driven total summaries
sections.text: Demand-driven total summaries totalSummary is a demand-driven part of the loadData(args) contract. Thegrid includes it only when the total footer needs to be loaded or refreshed.When the property is absent, a remote data source should skip the aggregatequery and omit DataResult.totalSummary from its response. When args.totalSummary is present, the returned values must describe thecomplete filtered result, not only the current page or the currently expandedgroup. The request may contain more than one summary, including differentsummary types for the same field: This keeps paging and aggregation independent: dataItems may be one page,while totalSummary represents the whole filtered dataset.

Custom remote source Implement loadData() to connect a view to an API. This example uses a simulatedendpoint with a short delay, so it runs without a server. The source is read-only:it deliberately supplies no mutation methods.

sections.title: Paged product catalog
sections.text: Paged product catalog Enter a product-name filter and press Enter or Search. Use Next andPrevious for paging. Rapid searches cancel the previous request; only the latestresponse can update the display. Simulate request error rejects the next loaduntil unchecked; Retry repeats the current query. Filtering is performed before count calculation and paging. The count thereforedescribes all matches, even though only three products are displayed at once.The source handles flat filtering and paging only; sorting, grouping and summariesare intentionally not implemented by this minimal endpoint. API: DataSource.loadData,QueryArgs, DataResult.

sections.title: Replace the simulated endpoint
sections.text: Replace the simulated endpoint Keep the source contract and replace the local request function with your HTTP client: This snippet assumes your endpoint accepts these query fields and returns{ items, totalCount }. Validate and translate them on the server; do not concatenateclient-provided filters into SQL. Add support for sorting, grouping and summarieswhen those capabilities are needed by the consumer.

sections.title: Cancellation and stale results
sections.text: Cancellation and stale results Cancellation saves unnecessary work when supported by the transport. The identitycheck also prevents stale responses from repainting the screen if a source doesnot honor cancellation. Clear loading state only for the current request.Abort the active request when the consumer is destroyed. API: QueryArgs.abortSignal.

sections.title: Add editing only when supported
sections.text: Add editing only when supported An editable source can add update, delete, createNewRow and changed.The source owns persistence and new-row session behavior. A read-only implementationdoes not need to provide placeholder methods that always reject. See DataSource overview for the editing contract,or DataSet for collecting local changes before a batch save.
New-row sessions These examples use the orders table fromTables, rows and change tracking. The session belongs tothe source; DataGrid’s session commandsadd checks for retained invalid UI input.

sections.title: New-row sessions
sections.text: New-row sessions API: DataTable.createNewRow(), update(), NewRowSession: insert(), cancel(), state; DataRow.table, isPending. Pending rows are excluded from queries, counts, summaries and save payloads. Severalsessions can coexist. Rules for a pending row may edit that row but not other rows.Insertion rules can update related rows after the session reaches the inserted state. Use row.isPending to check for a pending session without allocating and searching arow list. It becomes false on either insert or cancel and follows undo/redo and rollback.False alone does not guarantee membership: cancelled and removed rows are not pending. Insert and cancel are individually idempotent. Insert after cancel, or cancel afterinsert, rejects. A rejected insert leaves the session pending. Creation and cancellationfailures reject their Promises because those methods do not return MutationResult. Creation, field edits and local insert each have their own undo entry. Undoing creationcancels its session; redo restores the same row and session. Undoing insert makes itpending again.

Transactions and business rules The examples continue with the dataset and orders table fromTables, rows and change tracking. Try the completesales order example to see rules, local acceptance and saving together.

sections.title: Transactions
sections.text: Transactions An ordinary setValue(), update(), delete(), create, insert or cancel has its owntransaction. Group several operations explicitly when they represent one action: API: DataSet.transaction(), DataTransaction, DataEditContext: setValue(), update(), getTable(). All direct edits and their business effects become one undo operation. Before thefirst change to each affected row, the transaction records its values, acceptedvalues, state, membership and new-row session status. Changes are visible to reads while the transaction is running. UI notifications aredeferred until success; this is not read isolation. Unrelated writes, imports andsaves are blocked, including across await. Use the context to join the transaction. Validation rejection returns success: false. Exceptions reject the Promise.Both restore the complete edit and add no history. Rollback cannot reverse externalside effects: do not persist to the server from a business-rule subscription.

sections.title: Validation and business rules
sections.text: Validation and business rules rowChanging runs before an update, insertion, deletion or cancellation.rowChanged runs after the mutation, inside the same transaction, including new-rowcreation. Creation is reported after defaults and the identity are initialized. API: DataTable.rowChanging, rowChanged, DataRowChangeEvent: fields, values, reject(); DataRow.isPending, DataEditContext.setValue(). The event supplies kind, row, fields, oldValues, values and context. For updates,oldValues and values contain the affected fields. Values are readonly field containers,not cloned objects. reject() stops dispatch and rejects the complete transaction.

sections.title: Event kinds
sections.text: Event kinds Business events use DataRowChangeEvent.The following table describes events emitted by DataTable: kind Operation rowChanging rowChanged create A new pending row is initialized with its identity and defaults Not emitted Row is pending; use the context to initialize more fields update One or more field values actually change, including on pending rows Before applying the values After applying the values insert A pending session is inserted locally Row is still pending Row is confirmed and isPending is false delete A confirmed row is marked deleted, or an unsaved added row is removed Before deletion After deletion cancel A pending session is cancelled Row is still pending Session is cancelled and isPending is false For update, fields contains the names that changed. For the other kinds it isempty: detect the lifecycle operation using kind, not fields. Equal-value editsand repeated successful insert/cancel calls do not emit new events. The order-editor demo updates its header total on a line total change, insertionor deletion. Pending lines do not affect the header until insertion succeeds: API: DataRowChangeEvent.kind, DataRow.isPending, DataTable.rows, DataEditContext.getTable(), setValue(). For UI consumers, changed usesDataSourceChanged. It reports the same fivemutation kinds only after transaction success, plus reset for undo/redo,acceptance, rejection and nonempty imports. Business events never emit resetand never rerun during replay. A failed transaction emits no committed UI changes. The context operates on the actual dataset and rows. It provides getTable(), setValue(),update(), delete(), createNewRow(), insert() and cancel(). Do not call ordinaryrow.setValue() from a rule: it attempts an independent edit. A context expires whenthe transaction finishes.

sections.title: Asynchronous rules
sections.text: Asynchronous rules Business events use AsyncObservableEvent. Subscribers run sequentially in subscriptionorder, and their returned Promises are awaited. No waitUntil registration is needed. API: AsyncObservableEvent.subscribe(), DataTable.rowChanged, DataRow.getValue(), DataEditContext.setValue(). Await or return derived edits when subsequent rules depend on them. An exception stopslater subscribers and causes rollback. UI consumers should use changed instead: API: DataTable.changed, DataSourceChanged, ObservableEvent.subscribe().

sections.title: Cyclic rules
sections.text: Cyclic rules The context remembers the causal chain, including asynchronous continuations.A real change that re-enters the same row and field in that chain is rejected:quantity → total → quantity. Equal values are harmless, and independent sequentialedits to a field are allowed. Chains of more than 100 steps are also rejected.

Saving, accepting and rejecting changes Use the dataset from Tables, rows and change tracking.The openDrafts array below represents session references retained by yourapplication; it is not an implicit DataSet property. Seenew-row sessions for creating those references.

sections.title: Save, accept and reject
sections.text: Save, accept and reject The application owns persistence. Insert the pending sessions you want included,check their results, and then send the dataset’s batch: API: NewRowSession.insert(), DataSet.saveChanges(), DataSetSaveHandler, DataSetChanges, DataSetSaveChangesResult. The payload is grouped by table name. Insert entries include all values; updatesinclude changed fields; removals carry the key. Expected validation failures resolvewith success: false and optional fieldErrors. Transport failures reject. Temporary identities can be mapped without replacing DataRow objects: API: DataSetSaveChangesResult, KeyMapping. Mappings are validated before any is applied. Related foreign-key fields are notrewritten automatically. A successful save accepts all confirmed changes and clearsthis dataset’s history, preserving other coordinator scopes. Failed saves retainthe edits and history. For external persistence use acceptChanges(); for explicit discard use rejectChanges(): API: DataSet.acceptChanges(), rejectChanges(), NewRowSession.cancel(). Save, accept and reject throw while any pending session or unfinished creation remains.They never choose insert/cancel for the application. A nonempty import of refresheddata also clears the dataset history to prevent stale replay. A table-level accept,reject or import clears the whole dataset scope because entries may span tables.

sections.title: Undo and redo
sections.text: Undo and redo API: UndoCoordinator.undo(), redo(), DataSet.undoHistory, UndoHistory.canUndo, canRedo. Replay restores recorded row versions without rerunning business rules. Derivedvalues are already included in the recorded operation. UI observers receive a resetafter restoration. A new successful edit discards the coordinator’s global redo branch.Read UndoCoordinator for shared data/view histories.
Tables, rows and change tracking

sections.title: Create a dataset and tables
sections.text: Create a dataset and tables Create tables through the dataset so they participate in its save batch and transactions.Table names must be unique. Initial imported rows are accepted, with state unchanged.The identity field defaults to id; identities are strings or finite numbers. API: DataSet, createTable(), getTable(), DataSetOptions, DataTableOptions. defaults may be an object, a function, or an asynchronous function. The function runsfor every new row. createRowId can also be asynchronous, and a table-level generatoroverrides the dataset generator. The generated identity takes precedence over anidentity supplied in defaults.

sections.title: Read values and track edits
sections.text: Read values and track edits API: DataRow: setValue(), getValue(), getOriginal(), isModified(), toObject(), changes(); DataTable.getChanges(), MutationResult. Rows have four persistence states: State Meaning unchanged Accepted data without tracked edits modified An existing row was edited; transport includes differing fields added A new row not yet accepted after persistence deleted A confirmed row marked for removal Changing a field back to an equal accepted value removes that field from the updatepayload. The row may retain modified state even when getChanges() has no update for it.Deleting an unsaved added row removes it without creating a server delete request.

sections.title: Equality and object-valued fields
sections.text: Equality and object-valued fields The default comparison is Object.is. Objects, arrays and dates are stored by referenceand are not cloned. Replace a field value to track a change; modifying the contentsof the same object is not tracked or reversed by undo. API: DataSet.createTable(), DataTableOptions.equals. equals is synchronous and must be side-effect-free, reflexive, symmetric and transitive.It is used both to detect edits and to compare with accepted values. Equal values donot replace the existing reference, raise business events or add history.

DataSet A DataSet holds the working data for an application screen. Its named tables implementthe DataSource contract, while DataRow objects retain their identity across edits,rollback and undo/redo. Edits are local until the application saves the accumulated changes. Use it when several views should share pending edits, calculated fields and one datahistory. A remote source can still be used directly; a DataSet is useful when theapplication wants a local batch-edit workspace.

sections.title: Try an order editor
sections.text: Try an order editor The sales order has a header in salesOrders and its lines in salesOrderLines.Click Edit or Add line to open a form. OK accepts the form locally;Cancel discards its input. A business rule calculates the line amount and updatesthe total in the order header. One Undo reverses the accepted edit and both totals.Deleting a line also updates the order total and can be undone. Save order sends the accumulated changes to a simulated server. Successful savingaccepts the data, maps temporary line IDs and clears the data undo history. UnderBehind the scenes, enable Simulate server rejection to see a failed saveretain the local changes. A new line is pending until OK inserts it; Cancelcancels its session. Undoing insertion restores the draft: use Resume draft tofinish or cancel it before saving. Expand Behind the scenes to inspect the save payload and event log. Business entriesshow the transaction label, table, row ID and old → new field values, including derivedline and header totals. Lifecycle entries show the row values; committed UI notificationsshow the resulting row or table snapshot. Server entries include the request and ID mappings.Business events (“BEFORE” and “AFTER”) are distinct from committed UI notifications(“UI”). Their kind values are listed inEvent kinds. The contracts areDataRowChangeEvent andDataSourceChanged. The form keeps its inputs separate from the working data until OK. Editing anexisting line and inserting a new one share the same acceptance path: API: DataSet.transaction(),DataTransaction.update(),insert(),NewRowSession,MutationResult. Accepting the form does not contact the server. Save order later callsDataSet.saveChanges() with the completebatch from both tables. Cancelling an existing-line form needs no rollback becauseits inputs have not been applied; cancelling a new-line form callsNewRowSession.cancel().
