Fields and presentation Field definitions have three layers. Choose the smallest contract needed by theconsumer, and extend it when adding presentation or grid behavior. Contract Responsibility DataField Field name, semantic type, value access and grouping DataViewField Labels, description, display text, editor, lookup and per-row visibility DataGridColumn Width, alignment, resize/reorder, menus, cell styles and VNode rendering

sections.title: Data access
sections.text: Data access A DataField describes values in any row type.It does not register a field in a DataTable or require a DataSet. Local groupingand summary engines consume this contract without depending on a UI component. API: DataField.getValue,dataType,DataType. Declare dataType explicitly for numbers, dates and booleans. Missing types defaultto string when a type is required; an editor choice does not determine the type.Numeric summary evaluation can also recognize actual number values when no typewas declared.

sections.title: Reusable presentation
sections.text: Reusable presentation DataViewField extends DataField. It describeshow a field can be presented by a form, card, list or grid, without defining a columnwidth or depending on grid menu types. API: DataViewField.caption,getText,lookup,createEditor. dataType selects the standard editor. lookup supplies searchable choices andoptional result columns; createEditor provides a custom editor without changingthe semantic type. resolveText, validate, and formatValue describe conversion,validation, and editable formatting. Hosts pass row-bound callbacks to value-onlyeditors and save through their data source, never through field setters.See Cell editing for interactive examples. displayFormat is display-only: it preserves the raw value and editor precision.For regular labels the priority is getText, lookup, displayFormat, thenformatValue or string conversion. The grid also applies display formats togroup and total summaries, except counts. See Numbers, dates and formattingfor numeric patterns, literal currency suffixes and locale-aware parsing.

sections.title: Grid columns
sections.text: Grid columns DataGridColumn extends DataViewField with gridlayout and interaction. Reuse the common field definition and add grid options: API: DataGridColumn.width,textAlign,renderCell,customCellStyle. See Columns and layout andCustom cell rendering for live examples.
Text expressions and ranges

sections.title: Text expressions and ranges
sections.text: Text expressions and ranges DataFilter itself has no range operator. DataFilterRow translates a text expressioninto one or two comparisons, using the field’s semantic dataType: Text fields default to contains; other types default to equality.Explicit comparisons include =, !=, <, <=, > and >=.The text operator != becomes <> in DataFilter.Open-ended numeric and date ranges are inclusive at the supplied endpoint.Date parsing accepts the formats supported by DataFilterRow, including ISO datesand day.month.year. The keyword today represents the current local date at midnight.A date-only upper bound is midnight, not the end of that day;for datetime data use an appropriate exclusive upper bound for the following day. To search for literal operator-like text, start the input with a backslash.For example, the input \=abc means contains ‘=abc’, whereas =abc means equals ‘abc’.In a JavaScript string, escape the backslash: API: DataFilterRow.parse,DataType.

sections.title: Reverse conversion and readable text
sections.text: Reverse conversion and readable text fromFilter returns expressions only when the filter can be representedunambiguously as a collection of field/text pairs. OR, NOT, transformed selectorsand ambiguous conditions return false. A lower/upper bound on the same numericor date field is represented as one range expression.toText can display complex filters even when fromFilter returns false. API: fromFilter,toFilter,toText.

DataFilter DataFilter describes a condition or a tree of conditions as arrays. The samefilter can be evaluated locally, supplied to a DataSource or translated by a server.It contains no grid state and does not depend on a particular editor.

sections.title: Conditions and operators
sections.text: Conditions and operators A condition is [selector, operator, value]. A selector is normally a field name: Operators Meaning =, <> Equal / not equal >, >=, <, <= Ordered comparisons contains, notcontains Text includes / does not include startswith, endswith Text prefix / suffix In local evaluation, text operations are case-insensitive and treat null/undefinedas empty text. Equality with null matches null or missing (undefined) values,but not empty text (""); <> null matches values that are not missing.Remote SQL adapters translate these conditions to IS NULL / IS NOT NULL.Use null, not undefined, in serialized filter conditions.Other equality comparisons use strict JavaScript equality; objects and Dateinstances are compared by reference. Ordered comparisons use JavaScript comparison semantics.Supply values of the correct type rather than relying on coercion. API: evalFilter.

sections.title: AND, OR and NOT
sections.text: AND, OR and NOT Use explicit groups when exchanging filters with FilterEditor.DataFilter/evalFilter also support implicit AND and unary NOT independently ofthe editor’s supported UI structures.

sections.title: Evaluate locally or query a source
sections.text: Evaluate locally or query a source ArrayDataSource filters before counting and paging. A custom remote source mustimplement or translate the query itself; evalFilter is a local evaluator, not aSQL generator. Empty filters match all rows. Malformed expressions and unsupportedoperators throw errors instead of silently matching records. API: evalFilter,QueryArgs.filter.See DataSource.

sections.title: Transformed selectors and transport
sections.text: Transformed selectors and transport A selector can also describe a named transformation: Built-in local functions include date/grouping transformations such as year andmonth. Custom functions can be supplied through FilterFunctionRegistry.Remote sources must explicitly support the same named transformations. API: FilterSelector,FilterFunctionRegistry. Field names, operators and groups can be serialized as JSON. Date values becomestrings during JSON serialization; the receiving application must restore orinterpret their types. In particular, local evaluation of Date bounds requiresDate-compatible values rather than an unprocessed JSON string. For grid-specific interaction, see DataGrid filtering.

Numbers, dates and formatting Use formatters outside the UI for consistent display and parsing. DateEditor, TimeEditor and DateTimeEditor keep canonical strings, not JavaScript timestamps. Date-only values have no timezone. These formats are a documented .NET-inspired subset, not full .NET compatibility.

sections.title: Numeric formats
sections.text: Numeric formats NumberFormatter implementsValueFormatter without a UI dependency. Constructit once and reuse it; each instance retains its Intl formatters. Patterns arecase-sensitive. An optional precision specifies fraction digits, from 0 to 20.N, F, P and currency patterns default to two fraction digits; G accepts noprecision and does not impose a fixed number of decimals. Pattern Meaning Example with en-US G General, no grouping or forced trailing zeros 1234.56789 → 1234.56789 N0 Grouped, no fraction digits 1234.56 → 1,235 N2 or N Grouped, two fraction digits 1234.5 → 1,234.50 F2 or F Two fraction digits, no grouping 1234.5 → 1234.50 P1 Percentage, one fraction digit 0.125 → 12.5% P Percentage, two fraction digits 0.125 → 12.50% C$ Grouped amount and literal dollar sign 1234.5 → 1,234.50 $ C€ Grouped amount and literal euro sign 1234.5 → 1,234.50 € CBGN Grouped amount and literal currency code 1234.5 → 1,234.50 BGN C0€ Currency, no fraction digits 1234.5 → 1,235 € C2BGN Currency, two fraction digits 1234.5 → 1,234.50 BGN

sections.title: Currency and locale
sections.text: Currency and locale Currency suffixes are an Elgora UI extension, not standard .NET currencysyntax. Use C, optional precision, then one or more letters or currencysymbols, without spaces: C2€, C$, CBGN. Bare C/C2 are invalid.The suffix is literal: $ does not infer USD, and no exchange conversion occurs.The suffix always follows the number, separated by a nonbreaking space, evenwhere a locale would normally put currency before the amount. Locale controls decimal/group separators, grouping sizes, minus signs and percentplacement. Omit it to use the runtime locale. Digits remain Latin. G retains upto 21 significant digits without scientific notation; it is not .NET’s Gexponent-selection algorithm. Custom numeric masks, hexadecimal formats,accounting negatives and quoted literals are not supported. format() requires a finite JavaScript number; it rejects strings, NaN andinfinity. parse() accepts the configured locale, with or without digit grouping,and trims surrounding whitespace. Regular spaces, NBSP and narrow NBSP areinterchangeable where the locale uses space separators. Grouping must be valid;F/G do not accept grouped input. Currency/percent affixes must be present.Empty input, other currencies, exponents, trailing text and malformed numbersthrow. Nullable/empty handling belongs to the editor. Parsing does not requirethe configured number of fraction digits.

sections.title: Display formats on fields and columns
sections.text: Display formats on fields and columns Set displayFormat on a DataViewField or DataGridColumn, together with anoptional locale. This currently supports dataType: "number" anddataType: "date" (using DateFormatter patterns). Use getText for other types,including combined datetime labels. Normal cell label precedence is getText → lookup.getValueText →displayFormat → formatValue → string conversion. Null/undefined display asempty text when formatted. Field formatters are cached per field and recreatedwhen its pattern, locale or data type changes. The grid resolves locale in thisorder: column → grid → the grid’s application context or Localization.default→ runtime locale. A locale change repaints built-in formatted labels and summarieswithout re-querying data. Explicit column/grid locales remain overrides.Use setColumnOptions to change column metadata. getText and lookup labelsremain application-owned; custom callbacks are not automatically rerun when thelocale changes. See Localization. The grid applies the same display format to group and total aggregate values,without changing raw source results. count and distinct remain plain counts,not currency/percent amounts. Custom numeric aggregate results use the field’sformat; custom textual results remain text. Summary labels do not callrow-dependent getText, lookup resolvers or formatValue. See the DataGrid overview for grouped integers,decimal prices and euro totals using the same patterns in data rows and summaries.

sections.title: Display is not editing
sections.text: Display is not editing displayFormat never changes the stored value, sort/group keys or aggregateprecision. It does not configure an editor’s parser. A value of 1234.56789displayed with N2 is rounded visually, but its numeric editor still receivesthe original 1234.56789. formatValue remains the explicit editable-text hook. If an editor must accept localized numeric input, provide a matchingresolveText explicitly. For example, a standalone NumberEditor can use aformatter for input as well as output: This explicitly chooses a two-decimal editing representation. Parsing a roundedlabel cannot recover the original hidden decimals; avoid lossy editor formatswhen full precision must remain editable. Copying a formatted grid label likewiseproduces display text: configure a field’s resolveText if pasted localized orcurrency text should be accepted. Numeric formatting uses JavaScript numbers,not an arbitrary-precision decimal or financial arithmetic engine.

sections.title: Resolve and format text
sections.text: Resolve and format text Set dateFormat to use the same pattern for display and parsing: Supported custom tokens are d/dd (day), M/MM (month) and yyyy(four-digit year). Each field must appear exactly once with non-alphanumericseparators between fields. dd and MM require two input digits; d and Maccept one or two. Separators must match exactly; surrounding input whitespaceis ignored. Empty editor input means null. The single-letter standard format "d" uses the locale’s short-date layout: The default is "yyyy-MM-dd". This is a .NET-inspired subset, not full .NETcompatibility: month names, two-digit years, time tokens, quoted literals andother standard formats are not supported yet. Unsupported patterns fail atconstruction, even when custom callbacks are supplied. Dates remain Gregorianwith Latin digits, independently of the locale’s default calendar. The standalone DateFormatter implementsValueFormatter without UI or saving dependencies: Unlike lossy numeric display formats, the supported date formats preserve thecomplete date. Invalid calendar dates are rejected rather than normalized. The default conversion trims whitespace, maps blank input to null, and rejectsinvalid dates such as 2026-02-29, ambiguous formats or timestamps. Businessvalidate and onCommit are not invoked by resolveText(). Use a paired resolveText/format (or parse/format) for another input format.An explicit format overrides dateFormat display. resolveText, then parse,override dateFormat parsing; the other direction continues using dateFormat.Keep custom converters paired consistently so calendar choices can be parsed too.Custom conversion may be asynchronous, but must return canonical ISO dates ornull; it cannot bypass calendar bounds. The input and calendar trigger retain their DOM identity. The trigger uses keyedVNodes and frame-batched rendering, while DatePicker owns and patches its own view.

sections.title: Time formats
sections.text: Time formats TimeFormatter formats and parses canonical time strings. See Time and DateTime for supported patterns, precision and picker behavior. Use the same converter pair for display and input; a localized label is not automatically a reversible input format. API: NumberFormatter, TimeFormatter, DateFormatter, ValueFormatter.
Choose a data model The data layer can be used without DataGrid. All three models can feed a grid, a form or an application-owned view.

sections.title: A small local list
sections.text: A small local list Use ArrayDataSource around existing objects. It queries and mutates the supplied array, preserves object identity and emits change notifications. It does not provide batch saving or undo history. Use mutation methods, or explicitly invalidate caches after external changes.

sections.title: Backend-owned data
sections.text: Backend-owned data Implement the DataSource contract when the backend owns filtering, sorting, paging and acceptance. Start with the custom remote source example. Only loadData is required; advertise mutation and history capabilities only when implemented.

sections.title: A local editing workspace
sections.text: A local editing workspace Use DataSet for tracked DataRows, related tables, transactional business rules and undo. Tables implement DataSource, so views consume them directly. New-row insertion is local; saving and accepting changes are separate commands.

sections.title: Keep responsibilities separate
sections.text: Keep responsibilities separate Fields define value access, presentation, conversion and lookup metadata. Editors manage input, validation and an external acceptance callback. Sources query and mutate working data. DataGrid owns visual navigation, selection, editing and retained invalid input. Start with the simplest model that fits. A grid does not require a DataSet, and adding one later does not require a different grid query protocol.

Rendering and VNodes Use native elements for static structure, bindings for small observable projections, and VNodes when a changing subtree is easier to describe declaratively. You do not need to rebuild a complete screen for every state change.

sections.title: Schedule a small rendering task
sections.text: Schedule a small rendering task Component.render schedules work through the Elgora UI scheduler. Repeated requests for the same task can be coalesced within a frame. Keep the task function stable instead of allocating a new closure for every update. Component.renderOnChange subscribes to an ObservableValue and registers cleanup with its owner. For a single text, property, attribute or style, prefer the binding methods. They already participate in scheduled rendering and release their subscriptions on disposal.

sections.title: Describe changing content with VNodes
sections.text: Describe changing content with VNodes The v factory describes elements without creating a new live DOM tree on every call. Component rendering can patch that description into its owned content. Keys identify logical siblings across changes; use stable domain IDs, not array positions when the list can reorder. DataGrid.renderCell accepts a VNode: the grid owns the cell wrapper and patches the returned content. See custom rendering for a working example. DatePicker and Forma demonstrate larger stateful components.

sections.title: Ownership and patching boundaries
sections.text: Ownership and patching boundaries Do not imperatively replace children that a VNode renderer owns. Likewise, avoid controlling the same class through both declarative props and a binding. Props combine class, className and ui, and remove only obsolete declarative classes while retaining unrelated classes. Scheduling batches UI work, not business transactions. Await data operations explicitly; use DataSet transactions when changes must succeed or roll back together. Measure layout after the relevant render has run, rather than assuming a scheduled update is synchronous.

Elements and components

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Overview ElgoraUI is a browser-native framework for building self-contained web apps. Its foundation is a small set of composable components, native DOM elements, observable state, explicit events, and a token-based UI style system. The examples on this page are live and editable. They use plain JavaScript and run directly in the browser, so the code you learn here is also the code you can use in an ordinary HTTP-served application. The playground exposes the common ElgoraUI factories directly, so one-off elements can be composed without an Elgora. prefix.

sections.title: Elements and components
sections.text: Elements and components Use e() when you need a native DOM element. Use a Component or a c* factory when the element should have component state, lifecycle, rendering, or bindings. The c* factories create Component instances, while e() creates native elements when a component lifecycle is not needed. Both accept normal DOM properties and children. A component can be mounted into any ordinary DOM element; no application-wide runtime object or template compiler is required.

sections.title: What each part does
sections.text: What each part does e() creates ordinary DOM elements for the static heading and paragraph. cdiv() and cbutton() create Components. The app owns the button appended to it. ui composes library classes: box supplies the frame, p-3 adds padding, andd-flex / flex-col / gap-2 arrange the children. Styles are separate from behavior. app.observable(0) creates an ObservableValue owned by the panel. Updating Valuenotifies its subscribers. bindProperty projects the count into the button label through the UI scheduler.The binding is disposed with its component. mount() attaches the component tree and runs its mount lifecycle. These are the same primitives used by the larger library components; no app-wideruntime object or template compiler is needed.

Buttons

sections.title: Buttons
sections.text: Buttons button.elg keeps the native element predictable and flat. Add btn for the component styling, then choose a semantic role such as primary, neutral, or danger. The demo below includes all six semantic roles: primary, accent, neutral,success, warning, and danger, alongside flat and disabled buttons.“Anchor as button” is an <a> styled as a neutral button; “Text link →” is aplain navigation link, using the primary text color and an underline on hoveror keyboard focus. Both links open an example destination in a new tab. For a neutral action without a resting fill or visible frame, combine btnwith btn-ghost. Unlike a bare button.elg, it retains the standard buttonpadding, radius, hover/pressed feedback, disabled treatment and keyboard focusoutline. Its border stays transparent rather than changing the button’s size;an explicit selected state still shows its selection background. Plain and neutral buttons have a faint neutral background, a subtle border andneutral hover/pressed fills. Semantic roles such as primary and danger stayfilled; explicit surfaces and selected keep their own backgrounds. Keyboardfocus uses the shared outline. Native disabled buttons are dimmed and do notreceive hover/pressed styling. An aria-disabled link is styled the same way,but the application must prevent its activation. The defaults are --elg-btn-radius: 6px and --elg-btn-padding: .15em .5em.Override these on a container or individual button for a denser layout.--elg-btn-neutral-bg, --elg-btn-neutral-hover-bg,--elg-btn-neutral-pressed-bg and --elg-btn-neutral-border control the neutralappearance. The resting/hover/pressed defaults mix the theme text color at 3%/6%/10% overtransparency, so they work on both themes. Reduced motion disables transitions.

sections.title: Standard text links
sections.text: Standard text links Ordinary anchors with href use --elg-link-color, which defaults to the theme’sprimary foreground color. Visited links keep that same color. Links are notunderlined at rest; hover and keyboard focus add an underline. Keyboard focusalso shows the shared focus outline. The underline offset defaults to .18emthrough --elg-link-underline-offset. The same defaults apply to plain HTML and e(“a”, …). Explicit color utilitiesstill override the default. The btn style keeps its own treatment; no-underlineopts out of the text-link underline behavior for custom navigation. Anchorswithout href are not styled as interactive links.

Containers and typography

sections.title: Containers, sections and typography
sections.text: Containers, sections and typography Use the same classes with e(), c() or plain HTML. No Section or Herocomponent is required. Combine them with the existing responsive grid. UI style Purpose container Centered content with a maximum width, responsive gutters and border-box sizing. section Fluid vertical section spacing. title-display Large, fluid hero typography. title-section Fluid section headings. lead A comfortable introductory text size and line height. measure Limits reading width to 62 characters. eyebrow Small, spaced uppercase section labels. Override --elg-container-width (default 74rem), --elg-container-gutter(clamp(1rem, 4vw, 2.5rem)) and --elg-section-space(clamp(3.5rem, 7vw, 6.5rem)) on a page or section. Typography does not force acolor scheme; use the normal semantic color tokens and utility styles.

sections.text: Related topics and API Layout and responsive grid for column spans and container breakpoints. Surfaces and gradients and Forma for complete composition. UiStyle lists the typed utility names.
Native inputs and tables Use native HTML controls when you need browser behavior and simple styling. For parsing, validation and asynchronous acceptance, use Value editors.

sections.title: Form controls
sections.text: Form controls Use ui: ["elg", "field"] on a native input, select, or textarea. elg suppliesthe base control colors, border, and focus indication; field adds padding,rounded corners, border-box sizing, and min-width: 0. It does not arrange theform or make the control full-width. Add w-100 when needed and use flex or theresponsive grid to arrange fields. Most native-control styling is opt-in through elg, while utility classes workindependently. The stylesheet also defines global body typography, and normalCSS inheritance still applies to unmarked elements. For richer controls withparsing and validation, see Value editors.

sections.title: Tables
sections.text: Tables Use table for the base table treatment. table-row-borders adds only horizontal separators, while table-bordered adds a border around the table and its cells. Apply these styles to the <table> element. table sets full width, collapsedborders, cell padding, and header text styling; border variants add separatorswithout changing the data or interaction behavior. To show cell boundaries as well, replace table-row-borders with table-bordered.

Layout and responsive grid Use the grid UI style to create a twelve-column CSS grid. No layout componentor JavaScript width measurement is needed for the layout itself.The layout class elg-grid is separate from the DataGrid component, whose rootclass is elg-data-grid.Use the same utilities with native e() elements, c() components or virtualnodes created with v().

sections.title: Resize the container
sections.text: Resize the container Change Container width below. The surrounding page stays the same width;the fields respond to their own grid container. A wide demo can scroll horizontallyinside the preview so the selected width remains independent of the browser width. The form uses full-width fields initially, two fields per row from 480px,three from 768px and four from 1024px. Address and Notes use different spans.The nested Contact grid responds to its own, smaller content area. It remainstwo columns at widths where the outer grid can show four.

sections.title: Basic grid
sections.text: Basic grid col-1 through col-12 determine how many of the twelve tracks an item spans.A direct child without a column class occupies all twelve tracks.Use gap-0 through gap-5 for spacing. The default grid has no gap.Tracks use minmax(0, 1fr), and direct children have min-width: 0 so theirintrinsic width does not force wider tracks. Oversized content still needs itsown wrapping, truncation or scroll behavior. API: UiStyle, e,cdiv.

sections.title: Container breakpoints
sections.text: Container breakpoints Class Applies when the grid content width is col-N Any width col-sm-N At least 480px col-md-N At least 768px col-lg-N At least 1024px N is an integer from 1 to 12. These are mobile-first overrides: a largerbreakpoint overrides the smaller one when both apply, independently of class order.They are container queries, not viewport media queries. Responsive classes are applied to direct children of the grid. A non-responsivecol-6 remains half-width even in a narrow dialog; choose col-12 col-sm-6 whenit should stack at smaller sizes. The actual classes have the usual prefix, for example elg-grid andelg-col-sm-6. Existing utilities without responsive variants remain unchanged;this first version provides responsive overrides for column spans only.

sections.title: Components and virtual nodes
sections.text: Components and virtual nodes v() returns a virtual node, not a DOM element. Pass it through the vnodesproperty rather than calling appendChild(view). Both native elements andrendered virtual nodes receive the same CSS classes. API: cdiv, v.

sections.title: Nesting and sizing
sections.text: Nesting and sizing Each grid declares the named inline-size query container elg-grid.An item’s responsive span uses the nearest ancestor with that container name,which is its direct parent grid. A nested grid is sized by its outer column,while its children query the nested grid’s width. Container queries use the grid’s content box: padding is not usable track width.Inline-size containment also means the grid does not provide its contents’intrinsic width to an auto-sized parent. Give a shrink-to-fit host, such as adialog, an explicit width or an appropriate available-width constraint. Do not reorder items just to change the visual layout: keep DOM order alignedwith reading order and keyboard navigation. The grid does not impose a scrollcontainer; place overflow-auto on the host that should own scrolling.
Motion and scroll reveal

sections.title: Revealing content on scroll
sections.text: Revealing content on scroll ScrollReveal observes marked elements. Itstarts CSS entrance animations when they enter the viewport; it does not tieanimation progress to each pixel of scrolling. Observations are batched throughthe Elgora UI scheduler, not a per-frame scroll listener. data-elg-reveal selects fade or fade-up; an empty value uses the configuredeffect (default fade-up). Targets reveal only once by default. Set once: falseto repeat after leaving/re-entering. stagger delays sibling targets, capped at240ms so long groups do not make readers wait. The default threshold is 15%. Pass root for a nested scroll viewport. Call refresh() after adding/removingtargets; the helper does not install a mutation observer or recreate your DOM.dispose() restores owned classes anddelays and disconnects observers/listeners. Register it with addCleanup(). The motion tokens are --elg-motion-duration (560ms),--elg-motion-easing (cubic-bezier(.2, .7, .2, 1)) and--elg-motion-distance (18px); --elg-reveal-delay can delay an individualtarget when sibling staggering is not configured. fade-up uses individualtranslate, leaving a component’s transform available for hover/scale effects.Do not simultaneously animate the same target’s opacity or individual translatefrom two systems; reveal a wrapper in that case. Animation styles release theirproperties after completion.

sections.title: Rotating disclosure icons
sections.text: Rotating disclosure icons Apply ui: ["rotate-on-open"] (or elg-rotate-on-open in plain HTML) to adecorative icon inside a native summary. It rotates 180° while its detailsis open, with a 180ms transition using --elg-motion-easing. For custom controls, put the icon directly inside a button witharia-expanded="true" or "false". The control must update that attribute andmanage the associated content; this utility only animates the icon. Reducedmotion disables the transition, but preserves the open-state rotation. Set --elg-open-rotation on the icon to customize the angle (default 180deg).TreeView uses 90deg to turn a right-facing chevron downward. Keep the icon’sDOM node when updating the state so the CSS transition can run.

sections.title: Accessibility and fallback
sections.text: Accessibility and fallback Content remains visible if IntersectionObserver is unavailable. The helper doesnot set aria-hidden or remove content from the document. Keyboard focus revealsits containing target. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce shows all targets withoutanimation, including when that preference changes while the page is open. Printstyles also show pending targets without animation. Keyboard-focused targetsappear immediately, without stagger delays.After opting out, once-only targets are not hidden again when motion is enabled. The helper also works on server-rendered HTML: without JavaScript, targets arevisible because the pending class is installed only by the helper. Forma itselfis a client-rendered component demo; it is not an SSR or SEO implementation. See ScrollRevealOptions for the completeobserver configuration and the Component lifecycle for resourceownership. The standalone showcase uses the same public library exports as theembedded preview; its branding and illustrations remain demo-specific.
UI styles and utilities

sections.title: UI styles
sections.text: UI styles Elgora UI styles are composable classes backed by CSS custom properties. The classes describe the visual role of an element, while theme tokens decide the actual colors and proportions. This separation makes an application’s markup stable when its visual theme changes. class, className and ui are combined into one declarative class set,independently of prop order. Duplicate class tokens appear only once. This behavioris shared by e(), c() and virtual nodes created with v(). When props are patched, only obsolete declarative classes are removed; unrelatedclasses added through bindClass() or classList are retained. Do not manage thesame class token through both props and a binding or imperative code.

sections.title: The elg base class
sections.text: The elg base class The ui array prefixes style names with elg-; the special elg marker stays unchanged.The marker is not added automatically and is not inherited as a class by children.Layout and spacing utilities work without it. Add elg for base surface/textrendering and opt-in native-control styles, alongside the relevant visual role: Use ui on both components and native elements. It keeps the style vocabulary consistent and lets the framework compose the final class list for you.

sections.title: Color system
sections.text: Color system Color classes such as primary, accent, success, and surface are semantic roles. They are resolved through CSS variables, so the same component can use a different palette without changing its JavaScript. To create a theme, override the same token variables in a named selector. Future theme tooling can package these definitions and switch them through a small controller:

sections.title: CSS utilities
sections.text: CSS utilities Utilities are small, composable classes for layout and spacing. They keep simple presentation close to the component declaration: Common utilities include d-flex, flex-col, items-center, justify-between, gap-*, p-*, m-*, text-muted, and related spacing, alignment, and display helpers. Utilities should solve layout concerns; semantic component classes should describe the component itself.

sections.title: Component classes: box, btn, and future additions
sections.text: Component classes: box, btn, and future additions Component classes are reusable visual building blocks. Today the main examples are: box — a border, radius and shadow; add a surface and padding separately. btn — button structure and interaction styling. primary, accent, success — semantic variants shared by components and elements. Compose them with elg and utilities: This list is intentionally open. As the style system grows, new classes should follow the same contract: predictable composition, semantic names, and theme-aware variables.

Semantic colors ElgoraUI uses semantic colors instead of hard-coded color names. The same primary or danger role adapts to the active theme, while the markup stays unchanged.

sections.title: Color roles
sections.text: Color roles The built-in roles are primary, accent, neutral, success, warning, and danger. Each role provides these tokens: Token Purpose --elg-<role>-bg Background or fill of the semantic element --elg-<role>-text Text and icon color on that background --elg-<role>-border Border, divider, or outline color --elg-<role>-color Standalone accent text or icon on a normal surface The matching semantic class sets the background’s base HSL values, the foregroundcolor, and the border color token. For example, ui: ["elg", "success", "p-2"]creates a filled success surface. The semantic class does not draw a border:add border, box, or btn when a visible border is needed. Use CSS variables through var(...) in style declarations, not as names inthe ui array. For standalone colored text, use the text-* styles describedbelow.

sections.title: Theme-aware components
sections.text: Theme-aware components Use semantic classes for controls and containers so a theme switch changes the entire example consistently. The tokens are also available as CSS variables when a component needs a custom rule. Use semantic classes when the background and foreground belong together. Forcustom CSS, consume the corresponding variables explicitly: For standalone accents, use text-primary, text-success, or text-danger(for example, ui: ["text-danger"]). These consume the role’s *-color token,which can be lighter in the dark theme without changing filled button colors.text-neutral uses the neutral role’s text color for readable neutral text.

sections.title: Interaction and selection
sections.text: Interaction and selection The following UI styles change appearance; they do not implement selection,keyboard navigation, or application state themselves. UI style Visual behavior hover Adjusts the background while the pointer is over the element focus Adjusts the background when the element matches :focus-visible selected Applies the theme’s selection background and foreground active Adds persistent emphasis and an additional pressed-state adjustment Use an appropriate native element or ARIA pattern for the interaction. Thefocus style does not make a noninteractive element focusable. Native controlsmarked elg also have a focus-visible outline, independently of this backgroundstyle. Controls styled with btn already provide hover and pressed feedback.

sections.title: Applying a theme
sections.text: Applying a theme Set data-theme="dark" on the document element for an application-wide theme: The same attribute can be applied to a container to create a dark region insidea light page. Add elg to an element that should paint the themed background;the theme attribute defines tokens but does not paint a background itself.Derived color tokens are recalculated at the theme boundary. Popups followthe theme of their DOM ancestors; mount them inside the themed region whenusing a local theme. Native controls use the matching CSS color-scheme. Use --elg-bg-color, --elg-surface-color, --elg-text-color,--elg-text-muted, --elg-border-color, and --elg-border-strong for ordinarysurfaces. --elg-hover-bg supplies a subtle accent hover background;--elg-selection-bg, --elg-selection-text, and --elg-selection-borderdescribe selection. --elg-shadow-color adapts shadow strength to the theme.

sections.title: Customizing colors
sections.text: Customizing colors Override shared tokens rather than adding dark-theme rules to every component.The semantic classes derive their filled backgrounds from the role’s base HSLvalues. Set those values to customize a role across controls: Derived variables are recalculated at :root and elements with [data-theme].When overriding base HSL values locally, use a theme boundary as above; merelysetting them on an arbitrary descendant does not recalculate inherited derivedvariables. CSS rules that consume a final token directly can override that tokenat their scope instead. For example, --elg-success-color controls text-success;changing --elg-success-bg alone does not change the HSL-based success class. The built-in light palette is defined at :root, with overrides for[data-theme="dark"]. A nested data-theme="light" does not reset all valuesinherited from a dark ancestor; a locally inverted light region needs an explicitlight palette. Theme customization should also preserve foreground/backgroundcontrast and visible focus and selection states. Iframe documents have their own theme. The documentation previews synchronizethe docs theme automatically, including while an example is running. Continue with HTML elements to see these roles applied to native elements and controls.
Surfaces and gradients

sections.title: Containers and surfaces
sections.text: Containers and surfaces Use surface, surface-2, and surface-3 with elg to establish visual layers.box adds a border, rounded corners, and a shadow. It does not add spacing orchoose a background: combine it with a surface and p-* for inner padding.

sections.title: Gradients
sections.text: Gradients The existing gradient style accepts an angle and two colors. Its originalbackground-color defaults remain available through --elg-bg-color and--elg-bg-color-2. gradient-radial adds a soft spotlight; gradient-meshlayers three radial gradients. The mesh is a static CSS approximation, not acanvas or continuously running animation. gradient uses --elg-gradient-angle (default 300deg), --elg-gradient-fromand --elg-gradient-to. The radial variant also accepts--elg-gradient-position (default 50% 50%). Radial/mesh defaults derive fromprimary/accent tokens and transparency, allowing the underlying surface to showthrough. These styles set background images; they do not choose readable textcolors for arbitrary custom stops. Check text contrast in both themes.
